Title: Two men, including disabled mechanic, charged over Second Link race
Article:
KULAI: Two mechanics, including a disabled man, were charged in the magistrate's court here today with reckless and dangerous driving during an alleged illegal race on the Johor Second Link expressway last Saturday.
Mohamad Riduan Abd Ghani, 26, and Muhamad Aiman Izzuddin Shukri, 26, pleaded not guilty to the separate charges before Magistrate R. Salini.
The duo, who work as mechanics in Johor and Kuala Lumpur respectively, were alleged to have driven recklessly and dangerously, putting other road users at risk, at 7am on Aug 22.
The charge was framed under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, which carries a maximum five-year jail term, a fine of between RM5,000 and RM15,000 and a possible five-year suspension of the driving licence upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Lee Weng Hong led the prosecution, while Riduan and Aiman were represented by lawyers R.S. Amarpreet Singh and Abd Rahim Ali respectively.
The court granted each accused a RM5,000 with one surety and fixed Oct 5 for mention.
The charges followed a
police crackdown
after a 33-second video showing an alleged illegal race on the expressway went viral on social media.
The clip showed two riders racing while several people allegedly blocked the expressway to clear a path for them.
Some of those involved were also seen setting off firecrackers to celebrate after the race.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: CIMB advances tokenised sukuk push with RM1.68bil pilot
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: CIMB Group Holdings Bhd, through CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd, has completed a pilot to test the settlement of tokenised sukuk using tokenised deposits in a controlled environment.
The pilot involved a RM1.68 billion issuance under CIMB Islamic's existing RM10 billion senior sukuk wakalah programme, with tenures ranging from five to 15 years.
Of the total issuance, RM1.38 billion was represented in tokenised form and subscribed by 12 institutional investors, while the remaining RM300 million was issued as traditional sukuk.
Tokenisation allows financial assets such as sukuk to be represented digitally using distributed ledger technology, while tokenised deposits represent commercial bank money in digital form.
The bank said combining the two could enable greater automation and more integrated settlement of financial transactions, potentially reducing settlement delays, improving liquidity management and making fund movements more efficient.
CIMB Group Islamic Banking chief executive officer Ahmad Shahriman Mohamad Shariff said the initiative was driven by three key objectives namely promoting inclusivity, improving transparency and increasing efficiency in financial transactions.
He said digitalisation could make investments more accessible to smaller investors, while enhancing transparency by allowing funds be traced throughout the transaction process.
"This is also useful for Islamic finance, where we are very much asset-based or asset-backed," he said at a press conference.
Ahmad said tokenisation could also enable faster settlement, which would improve efficiency and help strengthen Malaysia's relevance in the capital market.
"Ultimately, all this will help move Malaysia forward in terms of our relevance in the capital market space," he said.
The pilot was conducted as part of CIMB's participation in Bank Negara Malaysia's digital asset innovation hub, which provides a controlled environment for financial institutions to test new digital asset applications.
CIMB is also engaging with the Securities Commission on the development of tokenised capital market products.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man admits assaulting elderly neighbour with metal rod
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A 62-year-old man today admitted in the Sessions Court here to assaulting his 86-year-old neighbour with a metal rod, leaving him seriously injured.
Ooi Hock Wah pleaded guilty to a charge under Section 326 of the Penal Code before Sessions Court Judge Irwan Suainbon.
Ooi admitted to committing the offence in front of a house at 326-F, Jalan Perak, here, about 9.30am on Aug 23.
The charge carries a maximum 20-year jail term, and the offender may also be fined or whipped upon conviction.
The court was told that the victim, Oung Kien Hock, remained hospitalised and was still receiving treatment.
Deputy public prosecutor Lee Jun Keong said the prosecution was not offering bail pending the tendering of the facts and sentencing, citing the victim's unstable condition and the risk of the accused, who is his neighbour, being released.
He said the 86-year-old victim was still receiving treatment at the hospital and that the investigating officer had informed them that both his legs and one arm had suffered fractures.
"For this case, the prosecution is not offering bail, taking into consideration, firstly, the victim's condition, which remains unstable and requires hospitalisation.
"Secondly, the accused is the victim's next-door neighbour, and granting him bail or releasing him could pose a significant risk in this case.
"Thirdly, the accused has pleaded guilty today. Therefore, Your Honour, we are seeking a date for the facts of the case to be tendered for sentencing," he told the court.
The court fixed Oct 1 for the facts of the case to be tendered and for sentencing.
Earlier, when the court stood down for a Chinese-speaking interpreter to read and explain the charge to Ooi, he suffered a seizure.
His condition stabilised after he took his medication.
Several people believed to be the victim's next of kin were also present in court to follow the proceedings and were seen exchanging words with the accused.
It was reported that the victim suffered serious injuries after he was allegedly assaulted with an iron rod by the suspect.
Northeast district police chief Assistant Commissioner Abdul Rozak Muhammad said
police received a report
on the incident at 9.55am, following an altercation at 9.30am.
The incident is believed to have stemmed from a misunderstanding between the victim and the suspect.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Factory operator claims trial over alleged rape, unnatural sex involving polytechnic student
Article:
BUTTERWORTH: A 22-year-old factory operator claimed trial at the Sessions Court today to raping and committing an unnatural sex act against a polytechnic student.
Muhammad Hazarul Zaim Rusli made the plea before judge Ooi Sheow Yean after the charges were read to him.
He was charged with raping the 20-year-old woman in a room at Golden Oriental Hotel, Jalan Kampung Benggali, at 3.30am on Aug 17.
The charge, under Section 376(1) of the Penal Code, carries a maximum 20-year jail term and whipping upon conviction.
On the second charge, he was accused of committing an act against the order of nature by penetrating the victim's anus without her consent at the same place, date and time.
The charge under Section 377C of the Penal Code carries a jail term of between five and 20 years and whipping, upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Muhammad Izad Firdaus prosecuted while lawyer RSN Rayer represented the accused.
In seeking bail, Rayer urged the court to exercise its discretion and set a reasonable amount, saying his client had just started working as a factory operator earning RM1,800 a month.
"My client is also responsible for caring for his parents, who are present in court," he told the court.
Rayer claimed the victim was the accused's girlfriend and maintained that the alleged incident had occurred with her consent.
"My client had been remanded for seven days and was willing to comply with additional conditions, including reporting to a police station twice a month," he added.
Izad objected to bail, citing the seriousness of the offences and concerns over the victim's emotional wellbeing.
He said the complainant was traumatised and feared the accused's release could make her feel threatened.
The court allowed the accused bail of RM10,000 with one surety for both charges.
The court also ordered him to report to the nearest police station every two weeks and prohibited him from contacting or interfering with the victim.
The case was fixed for mention on Sept 29 for the submission of documents.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Three friends, born in 1957, reunited for Merdeka
Article:
TUMPAT: For three former teachers, Merdeka celebrations carry a special meaning as they were all born in the same historic year — 1957.
Although none of the three best friends was born on Merdeka Day itself, their birth in the year Malaysia achieved independence has given them another reason to celebrate it with pride.
The trio, Wan Ahmad Khairuddin Wan Abdullah, Mat Salleh Mat Ail and Zulkifli Che Sulaiman, reunited at a Merdeka celebration organised by Kumpulan Dikir Barat Nagasari at Kampung Morak here last night.
Wan Ahmad Khairuddin, a former teacher at SMK Berangan, was born on Sept 10, 1957, while Mat Salleh, who taught at SMK A Falahiah, was born on Jan 14 the same year.
Zulkifli, a former teacher at SMK Tok Uban, was born on Nov 3, 1957.
The three friends, who have four to five children each, shared a special bond forged over the years, with their shared birth year adding another unique connection to their friendship.
For Wan Ahmad Khairuddin, growing up in the early years of independence meant witnessing first-hand how much the country had changed, particularly in terms of education and infrastructure.
He recalled that life was much simpler during his childhood, with fewer facilities and development compared with today. However, he said the changes over the decades had been remarkable, with better roads, schools, healthcare facilities and other amenities making life more convenient for Malaysians.
Mat Salleh said the transformation was particularly obvious in rural areas, where many places that were once surrounded by undeveloped land had gradually been transformed by new roads, buildings and other infrastructure.
As a former teacher, he said he was also proud to have witnessed improvements in the education system, with students today having access to facilities and technology that were unimaginable when he was young.
Zulkifli said the country had come a long way since he was born in 1957, with development taking place across the country and communities enjoying a much higher standard of living.
He said while the younger generation may take many modern conveniences for granted, those born in 1957 could appreciate the changes because they had experienced life before many of the developments took place.
Their reunion at the programme also offered a glimpse into a generation that grew up alongside the nation, witnessing Malaysia's transformation through the decades.
Now retired from teaching, the three remain enthusiastic about taking part in community activities and celebrating national occasions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal floods: 55 Malaysians uncontactable, no casualties confirmed
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Foreign Ministry has not received any official confirmation of Malaysian casualties following devastating floods in Nepal's Rasuwa district.
"At this stage, the ministry has not received any official confirmation of Malaysian casualties," it said in a statement today.
However, 55 Malaysian nationals reported to the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu are currently uncontactable following floods triggered by the overflowing Bhote Koshi River on Aug 26.

Title: Trial for accused mastermind of 9/11 attacks set for June 2028
Article:
WASHINGTON: A US Air Force judge on Wednesday ordered Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, the accused mastermind of the Sept 11, 2001, attacks on the United States, and three co-defendants to go on trial before a military tribunal in June 2028.
The trial-scheduling order entered by Air Force Lieutenant Colonel Michael Schrama marked the latest milestone in a military prosecution beset by two decades of legal deadlock surrounding the four detainees held in Guantanamo Bay, Cuba.
Last month, a US appeals court refused to allow Mohammed and two of his co-defendants to plead guilty under agreements that would have spared them the death penalty.
The appellate decision reversed decisions of a military judge and the US Court of Military Commission Review in support of the plea deal.
The agreement had been offered last year and accepted by the official who oversees the Pentagon's Guantanamo war court, only to be revoked last August by then-Defence Secretary Lloyd Austin amid criticism of the deal from Republican lawmakers.
Under Schrama's 11-page order, Mohammed and three co-defendants — Walid Muhammad Salih Mubarak bin 'Atash, Mustafa Ahmed Adam al Hawsawi, and Ali Abdul Aziz Ali — will stand trial starting on June 5, 2028.
The proceedings open with selection of a panel consisting entirely of service members who will act as the jury to hear the case according to rules of military justice.
Opening statements will commence 30 calendar days after the panel is seated, followed by presentation of the prosecution's evidence, after which the defendants may file motions for findings of not guilty.
The order gives both sides opportunities to argue those motions and rebut one another, and for prosecutors to reopen their case.
The defence presents its principal evidence starting 60 calendar days after the prosecution concludes its case.
The trial ends with a sentencing phase.
Schrama rejected the prosecutors' proposal to open the trial in January 2027, saying that would leave too little time for the "resolution of pretrial evidentiary and compliance motions."
Mohammed remains the most well-known inmate at the Guantanamo detention facility, which was set up in 2002 by then-US President George W. Bush to house foreign militant suspects following the Sept 11, 2001, attacks.
He is accused of orchestrating the plot to fly hijacked passenger jetliners into the World Trade Center in New York City and into the Pentagon.
The 9/11 attacks killed nearly 3,000 people.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ismail Sabri leaves court after son posts RM300,000 bail
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob has left the court complex after his son posted RM300,000 bail for him.
The 66-year-old Bera member of parliament declined to comment on the charge against him, saying he would leave the matter to his legal team, led by lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad.
Asked if he was in good health, Ismail Sabri replied: "Yes."
He later shook hands with and greeted supporters who had travelled from Bera to show their solidarity.
The supporters had lined up outside the court complex lobby and waited for more than two hours.
Also seen were former Umno Youth chief Khairy Jamaluddin and former Pahang Menteri Besar Tan Sri Adnan Yaakob.
Ismail Sabri was surrounded by supporters as he made his way to his car.

Title: Apparel group EMPG one step closer to Bursa listing, plans 15 new boutiques in two years
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Apparel group EMPG Group Bhd has secured Bursa Malaysia's approval-in-principle for its proposed listing on the ACE Market.
The company plans to use initial public offering (IPO) proceeds to expand its retail network, strengthen its multi-brand strategy and meet working capital needs.
The proposed IPO comprises a public issue of 121.6 million new shares and an offer for sale of 48.5 million existing shares.
Of the new shares, 30.3 million, or about five per cent of the enlarged issued share capital, will be offered to the public via balloting, with half reserved for Bumiputera public investors.
Another 4.3 million new shares, representing about 0.71 per cent, will be allocated to eligible directors and employees through pink form allocations.
A further 75.75 million new shares, or about 12.5 per cent, will be placed with selected Bumiputera investors approved by the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry.
A total of 11.25 million shares, or 1.86 per cent, will be offered via private placement to selected investors.
Under the offer for sale, 48.5 million existing shares, equivalent to about eight per cent of the enlarged issued share capital, will also be placed with selected investors.
Managing director Loh Tau Sing said the approval brings EMPG closer to the public capital market and positions it for its next phase of growth.
Loh said the IPO would fund the expansion of the company's retail network, strengthen its multi-brand positioning, upgrade its operational and logistics infrastructure and broaden its product offerings.
Under its prospectus exposure, EMPG plans to open 100 new consignment counters and 15 boutiques within 24 months of listing.
The new outlets will carry the Hummer and Pierre Cardin brands, alongside other existing brands.
EMPG designs, markets and sells apparel for men, women and children through consignment counters nationwide, standalone retail outlets in the Klang Valley and e-commerce platforms.
Its wholesale business covers outright sales as well as apparel and fabric sourcing services.
Its portfolio includes owned brands Exhaust, Idexer, Silverland, Brittania, Ventine, Millward, Aplus, John Rider, Oxen, Elmer and MU-7.
Berjaya Securities Sdn Bhd is the principal adviser, sponsor, underwriter and placement agent for the IPO.
Wyncorp Advisory Sdn Bhd is the corporate finance adviser.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Puchong residents saddled with infrastructure challenges
Article:
DEVELOPMENT has transformed Puchong beyond recognition. Unfortunately, its infrastructure does not appear to have kept pace.
At the heart of the problem is one of the busiest traffic arteries in the Klang Valley: the Lebuhraya Damansara-Puchong (LDP).
At many hours of the day, it is less an expressway than an enormous car park. A journey from Puchong Jaya to Sunway that should take five or 10 minutes can easily stretch to 40 minutes or an hour. Even getting to neighbouring Bandar Puteri can become an exercise in patience.
The problem is compounded by Puchong's location. It has effectively become a major conduit for traffic moving north, south and east.
The Sunway toll plaza does little to ease matters. Motorists trying to avoid the LDP by using the Bukit Jalil Highway frequently encounter similar congestion. Traffic entering the Kesas Highway also meets the same fate, with queues sometimes stretching for kilometres.
Over the past decade, Puchong sometimes feels less like an integral part of a city and more like its poor cousin — attached administratively, perhaps, but seemingly too far from the centre of attention to command sufficient urgency.
For residents, the frustration goes beyond traffic congestion. No matter which major route we take, tolls seem almost unavoidable. Toll-free alternatives exist, but the congestion, circuitous routes and other obstacles make them hardly worth the effort.
There are also smaller problems which may appear insignificant on a planning map but matter greatly to the people who encounter them every day. Along Persiaran Puchong Jaya Selatan, for example, there is a dangerous bend where accidents have occurred, and the road divider has had to be replaced several times over the years.
I had appealed to the Subang Jaya Municipal Council (MBSJ) to install warning signs to alert motorists to the bend. I was informed that the matter was not considered urgent and that there were other priorities.
That response is difficult to understand when road safety is involved.  On another occasion, I had complained about streetlights that frequently failed to work. Repairs were carried out, but I was subsequently given the contractor's contact details to deal with the matter directly if it recurred.
This raises another question: should residents have to pursue contractors themselves after reporting a municipal problem?
Then there was the case of the missing lamp-post. On Jan 1, 2026, a motorist crashed into a lamp-post at a traffic-light junction on a slope along Persiaran Puchong Jaya Selatan. As of Aug 26 — almost eight months later — the lamp-post has still not been replaced. Wires remain along the divider, with cones placed there to warn motorists.
Requests for additional traffic lights in the Puchong Jaya commercial area have similarly been rejected because the situation was deemed not urgent. One wonders what qualifies as urgent. There are junctions where road humps appear on only one approach to a four-way intersection, an arrangement that can leave motorists wondering about the logic behind the traffic-calming design.
Puchong Jaya also has problems with rats and crows. Individually, these matters may seem small. Collectively, they contribute to a larger impression: that residents complain, receive an acknowledgement or explanation, and then continue living with the same problem.
To be fair, Puchong is not alone. The massive traffic crawls around Sunway Pyramid, the infamous Kewajipan roundabout, and other parts of Subang Jaya are equally concerning. These long-standing congestion points also raise questions about whether development, traffic management, and road infrastructure have been allowed to grow out of balance.
Who exactly is responsible? Many of the highways are operated by private concessionaires. Local roads come under municipal responsibility. Other roads and junctions may involve state or federal agencies. Where one road system meets another, accountability can become blurred.
Development has brought enormous prosperity and transformation to Puchong. What was once plantation and mining country is now a thriving urban centre. But development cannot simply mean approving more buildings, commercial centres, condominiums and townships. Roads, drainage, public transport, traffic management, street lighting, cleanliness and public safety must grow alongside them.
We need the authorities and highway operators to look at the larger picture of what Puchong has become and what its infrastructure is being forced to bear.
SUSAI ANTHONY MUTHU
Puchong, Selangor
ends
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's business confidence rebounds sharply in Q3
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's business sector is turning more optimistic, with confidence improving sharply in the third quarter of 2026.
The overall business confidence indicator rose to 5.9 per cent in Q3 2026 from -1.8 per cent in Q2, according to the Statistics Department.
The quarterly Business Tendency Statistics tracks business expectations for the coming three and six months, based on the Business Tendency Survey.
All four major sectors expect business conditions to improve in Q3, with Industry recording the strongest rebound.
•        Industry: 8.2 per cent, up from -3.7 per cent
•        Services: 5.2 per cent compared with 6.2 per cent
•        Construction: 4.1 per cent, up from -9.5 per cent
•        Wholesale & Retail Trade: 1.2 per cent, up from -7.5 per cent
The department said the broad-based improvement reflects greater confidence in both domestic and external economic activity.
Business sentiment was positive in most states, with Terengganu recording the highest confidence indicator at 10.5 per cent, followed by Kuala Lumpur at 9.5 per cent and Negri Sembilan at 9.4 per cent.
Other states with positive readings included Pahang (7.1 per cent), Selangor (5.8 per cent), Sarawak (5.8 per cent) Perlis (5.4 per cent), Kedah (5.1 per cent), Pulau Pinang (5.0 per cent), Johor (4.9 per cent), Sabah (3.7 per cent), Kelantan (2.1 per cent) and Perak (1.5 per cent).
Putrajaya registered 0.6 per cent.
However, Melaka (-3.9 per cent) and Labuan (-5.4 per cent) remained pessimistic.
Businesses are also more upbeat about the second half of 2026, with the net balance climbing to 12.9 per cent, from 7.9 per cent for April-September 2026.
Construction businesses are the most optimistic, with a net balance of 23.3 per cent, followed by industry (14.3 per cent) services (13.1 per cent) and wholesale and retail trade (5.3 per cent).
Expectations for gross revenue are also positive.
Some 31.9 per cent of businesses expect revenue to increase in Q3, while 47.4 per cent expect no change and 20.7 per cent
anticipate a decline. This results in a net balance of 11.2 per cent.
Hiring sentiment is positive too, with 13.9 per cent of businesses expecting to increase their workforce, compared with 7.8 per cent anticipating reductions.
The resulting employment net balance stands at 6.1 per cent, while 78.3 per cent expect to maintain their workforce.
Separately, the department is conducting the Economic Census 2026 under the theme "Data Nadi Ekonomi Rakyat".
The sixth economic census runs from Jan 5 to Oct 31 2026 and aims to collect comprehensive data from registered and unregistered business establishments nationwide to assess Malaysia's economic performance, structure and characteristics.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Yayoi Kusama: Japan's kaleidoscopic, troubled 'polka dot queen'
Article:
TOKYO: The dotty pumpkins and kaleidoscope rooms of Yayoi Kusama, who has died aged 97, were as vibrant as the artist herself, but her exuberant work was the expression of a long battle with mental illness.
Once a fixture of the 1960s pop and minimalist scenes in New York, Japan's "polka dot queen" found huge commercial success in her later decades.
Her larger-than-life paintings, sculptures and installations – inspired by vivid hallucinations – sold for millions of dollars and packed out top galleries.
Kusama, instantly recognisable in her bright red wig and bold spotted outfits, worked well into old age from the psychiatric hospital in Tokyo where she lived voluntarily for the second half of her life.
But she also struggled with her feelings for her home country, which she left for decades and once described as "full of disdain for women."
Born in 1929, the youngest daughter of a wealthy but troubled family, Kusama began producing her signature dot and net patterns aged 10.
[[nid:1519738]]
"My mother had regrets about my birth, and I was driven to the edge psychologically," she wrote in her autobiography, "A Personal History of Polka Dots."
"One day, after seeing a tablecloth with a red flower pattern on a desk, I saw the same red flower pattern all over the ceiling, windows and pillars. It filled the room, and covered my body."
Art provided a release for the young Kusama, whose father, a seedling merchant, was unfaithful to her mother.
"When I was sad or lonely, everything would be cured when I drew pictures," she said.
In the book, Kusama explained her concept of "self-obliteration" – a recurrent theme throughout her career.
"I put dots all over my body and make all the surroundings dot patterns. By creating the same thing over and over, my own existence is buried in the art."
Kusama studied Japanese painting in Kyoto, against her parents' wishes, and held her first solo exhibition in 1952 in her hometown of Matsumoto in central Japan.
At the show, she met a psychiatrist who advised her to go and work abroad – an idea that appealed to her.
"Japan was so small, vulgar, feudalistic and full of disdain for women," said the artist.
"I was born and raised in Japan, but I'm not influenced by Japanese culture and tradition."
The decisive push to pack her bags came when she wrote to modernist painter Georgia O'Keeffe, who encouraged Kusama to seek international recognition in the United States.
Kusama moved to Seattle in 1957 and then to New York, where she struggled to find her place as an Asian artist in the city's largely white, male-dominated creative scene.
"I was at the lowest point of poverty. One time, I couldn't eat for three days because I had no money," she once told Japan's Asahi Shimbun newspaper.
"I even ate the breadcrumbs left by the pigeons."
But she persevered, and during her 16 years in New York became a prominent name in the avant-garde world.
At the height of the 1960s sexual liberation movement, she would stage "happenings", where people stripped naked on Wall Street or in Central Park and had their bodies painted with polka dots.
She also launched a fashion line, established a "Church of Self-Obliteration" and styled herself the "High Priestess of Polka Dots" to officiate at a gay wedding.
By the time she returned to Japan in 1973, however, Kusama was burned out and checked herself into a psychiatric ward where she lived for the rest of her life.
And it was not until the 1990s that her vivid patterns, bold floral shapes and shiny steel orbs hit the mainstream, later providing the backdrop to countless selfies.
Pumpkins are her most famous motif, featuring heavily in her paintings and giant sculptures.
The artist called them her "life partners", saying she had first grown to love their "generous, unpretentious looks" as a child.
Kusama was named the world's most popular artist in 2014 by The Art Newspaper.
She was also one of the most expensive, with one of her "infinity net" paintings fetching nearly $8 million at a 2019 auction.
But fame and fortune did not affect her remarkable originality, which she once attributed to the "serenity of the soul" that comes from spending time alone.
"Creative thinking is born of loneliness... because I stood before the art all alone, I was able to forge my own path," Kusama said.
She published several novels in her later years, while her exhibitions continued to draw huge crowds.
"My wish after my death is that the eternally bright future, the beauty of human love and my soul will be passed on," Kusama told reporters in 2017.
"Please love my artwork, even after I die."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mydin halts sale of Jalur Gemilang-themed tudung over star design error
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Mydin has ordered all its outlets to immediately stop selling a Jalur Gemilang-themed tudung after a customer flagged an apparent error in its 14-point star design.
Mydin said the error was caused by a printing mistake by its supplier, adding that it was taking action to prevent a recurrence.
"We apologise for the oversight and appreciate the feedback," the retailer said.
The issue surfaced after a Threads user, @faizfaisal.png, spotted the product at Mydin's Subang Jaya outlet and questioned how it had gone on sale.
The user said the star design could be perceived as disrespectful to the Jalur Gemilang and questioned the retailer's checks before the product was placed on sale.
"Mydin should take responsibility and explain how the design had passed its checks and recall the affected products," he urged.
The post, accompanied by photographs of the tudung, gained traction on social media, drawing attention to the apparent error in the Jalur Gemilang design.
Mydin's decision to halt sales follows the customer's complaint, with the retailer saying action would be taken to ensure a similar mistake does not recur.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Amir Hamzah on shaping Malaysia's next-gen financial system
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's next-generation financial system must balance innovation with trust, efficiency, resilience and stability as emerging technologies reshape the sector, said Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
The Finance Minister II said technologies such as artificial intelligence, digital infrastructure and tokenisation would create new opportunities for the financial and capital markets.
"However, their true value lies not in their novelty, but in their potential to improve market efficiency, reduce friction, expand access and create greater economic opportunity."
He said this at CIMB Group Holdings Bhd's
announcement of Malaysia's first tokenised deposit settlement for tokenised sukuk.
Amir Hamzah said Malaysia must therefore build a financial system that is more efficient, connected and inclusive, while strengthening the country's competitiveness and supporting future economic growth.
This was particularly important as technology continued to reshape global markets, investor expectations evolved and competition for capital intensified.
"We must build a financial system that is more efficient, more connected, more inclusive and better positioned to support Malaysia's future growth and competitiveness," he said.
This requires more than adopting new technologies; it also means strengthening market foundations, improving efficiency, widening access to capital and supporting sustainable economic growth.
"Malaysia enters this next phase from a position of strength. Over the decades, we have built deep, well-regulated and diversified capital markets.
"We have established global leadership in Islamic finance, and earned the trust of investors through strong institutions and sound governance and prudent regulation," he said.
Amir Hamzah said these achievements resulted from strong partnerships between regulators and industry, as well as the public and private sectors.
This spirit of collaboration will become even more important as the financial landscape evolves, noting that no single institution can shape the future of finance alone.
This will require strong regulatory leadership, responsible innovation, investor confidence and close cooperation across the financial ecosystem.
"The strong partnership of regulators, financial institutions, market infrastructure providers, institutional investors, government-linked investment companies, asset managers and corporates reflects a collective commitment to Malaysia's financial future," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 17 Malaysians travelling together with Nepal agency remain uncontactable
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Seventeen Malaysians on a trip organised by a Nepal-based tour agency are uncontactable following devastating flash floods in Nepal's Rasuwa district.
Fishtail Tours & Travels representative Roshan Panday said the group was travelling together and was last known to be near Timure, close to the Nepal-China border.
He said an agency colleague last contacted one of the group members at 8.18am local time as they approached the border.
He confirmed that all 17 Malaysians were travelling together when contact was last established.
""They were travelling together. A total of six cars, but together," he told the New Straits Times.
Roshan said the agency had been trying to locate the group, but efforts were hampered after roads were swept away by the floods.
"There is no road access as everything was swept away," he said.
He said helicopters were deployed yesterday in the search, while drones were also being used to locate the group.
Roshan said rebuilding roads in the affected area could take at least a year, meaning aerial access is the only way to reach the area for now.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Khaled: Don't boycott National Day celebrations over Rohingya issue
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The public should not boycott National Day celebrations over sentiments surrounding the Rohingya issue, said Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin.
He said Independence Day celebrations should not be driven by emotions or sentiments over specific issues affecting the country.
"Malaysia is the land where our blood was shed. Malaysia is our home. We should not stop caring for and beautifying our home simply because we disagree with the presence of those whom we did not invite.
"So, do not miss the opportunity to express our love and affection for our homeland simply because we are dissatisfied with certain issues affecting our country.
"Instead, use this space and opportunity to strengthen our love for our country.
"At the very least, our burning patriotism will serve as an indication to everyone, both within and outside the country, that Malaysians will not allow their homeland to become a political battleground or a platform for anyone's polemics," he said in his speech at the launch ceremony for the Jalur Gemilang flag-waving campaign.
Previously, some social media users had called on Malaysians to boycott National Day celebrations or attend the Putrajaya event carrying banners containing sarcasm or demands related to the Rohingya issue.
The social media users said Malaysians should not remain silent and should use the celebration as an opportunity to voice their concerns as the main stage would be occupied by national leaders.
Khaled also urged Malaysians to use this year's celebrations as an opportunity to reaffirm their commitment to safeguarding the country's sovereignty.
"This country did not gain independence and stand on its own. We must work together to develop it, protect it, cherish it and safeguard its sovereignty.
"Let this year be the year we make a commitment. A commitment not to do anything that could tarnish that sovereignty.
"Most importantly, let us never forget to pray for the well-being of this country, pray for the servicemen who fight and sacrifice at the front lines, and pray for all Malaysians," he said.

Title: Ipoh cannabis plant case: Wireman acquitted after prosecution fails to prove case [WATCH]
Article:
IPOH: A wireman was acquitted and discharged by the Sessions Court here today of a charge of allowing a cannabis plant to be cultivated at his home three years ago.
Aszizi Ayub, 37, was cleared of the charge at the close of the prosecution's case after the court found that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against him.
Judge Meor Sulaiman Ahmad Tarmizi, in his decision, said the court had evaluated the evidence presented by the prosecution and the submissions made by the defence.
"The court finds that the prosecution has failed to establish a prima facie case against the accused. Therefore, the accused is acquitted and discharged of the charge," he said.
According to the charge, Aszizi had allegedly allowed a 253.4-gramme cannabis plant to be cultivated at a house in Taman Dato Leow Yan Sip here on July 31, 2023.
He was accused of permitting the plant, which could be used to obtain cannabis, to be planted and cultivated by another person in a black plastic bag.
The offence was alleged to have taken place at 8.30pm at a house in Persiaran Wira Jaya Timur 36, Taman Dato Leow Yan Sip.
Aszizi was charged under Section 6B(1)(c) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, punishable under Section 6B(3) of the same Act, which prohibits the planting or cultivation of specified plants, including poppy, cannabis and coca plants.
The offence carries a mandatory punishment of life imprisonment and whipping of not less than six strokes.
Deputy Public Prosecutor S.S. Pavitra prosecuted, while Aszizi was represented by lawyers Keshvinder Singh, Sukhdave Singh and Renver Singh.

Title: Malaysia to lead Asean green jobs agenda for 2026-2030
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia will continue to lead Asean's green jobs agenda for 2026-2030 after being entrusted with regional projects under the Asean Labour Ministers' new work programme.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the role was established under the Asean Labour Ministers' Work Programme 2026-2030, building on Malaysia's mandate to drive the agenda, as it chaired the Asean Labour Ministers' Meeting (ALMM) and the Senior Labour Officials Meeting in 2018.
"The transition to a green economy cannot be viewed solely from an environmental or investment perspective. We must ensure the Asean workforce has the skills needed to fill new jobs.
"At the same time, the transition must be fair and inclusive so economic changes leave behind no workers or groups," he said in Malaysia's intervention at the 29th ALMM in Bangkok yesterday.
Ramanan said Malaysia had delivered two key green jobs documents under its 2025 Asean Chairmanship: the Asean Framework and Action Plan (FAP) for a Just and Inclusive Transition to Green Jobs 2025-2030 and the Joint Statement on an Actionable Plan for Green Jobs Towards a Sustainable and Inclusive Asean Workforce.
He said the documents set strategic directions for managing workforce changes arising from the green transition while strengthening regional cooperation to build a future-ready workforce.
Ramanan also highlighted Malaysia's successful hosting of the Asean Green Jobs Forum (AGJF) 2025 in Putrajaya, which attracted more than 450 delegates under the theme "AI, Digitalisation and Green Jobs".
He said the forum moved regional discussions beyond policy towards concrete implementation, including developing an Asean green jobs and skills taxonomy aligned with the Asean Qualifications Reference Framework and using artificial intelligence to support training and skills development.
Other priorities included modernising technical and vocational education and training through closer industry collaboration, providing targeted environmental, social and governance support for micro, small and medium enterprises, and expanding access to green jobs for women, youth and informal workers.
Ramanan said the efforts would help integrate green jobs into Asean workforce development amid technological, digital and industrial transformation.
Malaysia also expressed support for the Philippines, which will host AGJF 2026 in Manila this October.
Ramanan said rotating the forum among Asean chairing countries would make the green jobs agenda a shared responsibility.
"Malaysia is ready to cooperate closely with the Philippines to ensure AGJF 2026 produces meaningful action in implementing the Asean Framework and Action Plan 2025-2030," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SoftBank in talks to buy stake in 1X at US$bil valuation
Article:
BENGALURU: SoftBank is in talks to buy a majority stake in OpenAI-backed humanoid robot developer 1X Technologies in a deal that would value the startup at about US$6 billion, The Information reported on Wednesday, citing people with knowledge of the deal.
Reuters could not immediately confirm the report. SoftBank Group and 1X did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.
The talks are ongoing, and the terms could change, the report said.
OpenAI and 1X last year discussed the possibility of the ChatGPT-maker acquiring 1X, the report added.
OpenAI invested in 1X in 2023 through its OpenAI Startup Fund, alongside Tiger Global and a group of Norway-based investors.
The 1X deal builds on SoftBank's broader push into robotics, following its agreement last year to acquire Swiss engineering group ABB's robotics business for US$5.4 billion.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Army ready to assist in flood-hit Nepal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Armed Forces are ready to contribute their expertise and capabilities to a humanitarian mission in flood-hit Nepal if called upon.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the armed forces were prepared to assist should the government decide that their capabilities were needed for the humanitarian response.
"We are ready. As we have stated, one of the things that the armed forces can contribute is in terms of humanitarian missions.
"If there is a decision by the government, and if it involves the armed forces , we are ready to contribute our expertise and capabilities," he said at a press conference at Wisma Pertahanan after the launch ceremony for the Jalur Gemilang flag-waving campaign.
His remarks came as Nepal faced severe flooding and mudslides near its border with China, with hundreds of people reportedly still missing, including more than 50 Malaysians who remain uncontactable.
Nepalese authorities earlier said a sudden flash flood had entered Nepal from the Chinese side via the Bhote Koshi River in Rasuwa district.
According to a Kathmandu Post report, 19 bridges and 40km of highway were destroyed by the floods.
Closed-circuit television footage showed buildings and vehicles at the Gyirong border port in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region being swept away by a torrent of water and mud.
Chinese President Xi Jinping has ordered all-out efforts to locate those missing in the region, China's UN ambassador Fu Cong said in a post on X.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nvidia agrees to buy Hugging Face for US$12.9bil
Article:
MEXICO CITY: Nvidia has agreed to buy Hugging Face, a repository of open-source AI models, for US$12.9 billion, The Information reported on Wednesday, citing a person with knowledge of the deal.
A deal of that size would mark one of Nvidia's largest acquisitions to date and underscore how the Jensen Huang-led company at the center of the AI boom is betting that demand for the technology is expanding rather than peaking.
It would also give Nvidia control of Hugging Face - which hosts open-source large language models and datasets - at a time when builders of closed-source models such as Anthropic and OpenAI are seeking to create their own chips as an alternative to Nvidia's graphics processing units.
The price tag would also stand in steep contrast to its annualized revenue of US$150 million reported by The Information earlier this week.
The chipmaker and New York-based Hugging Face did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment outside regular business hours. Nvidia was among companies such as Salesforce and Alphabet's Google that backed Hugging Face in a US$235 million funding round in 2023, valuing the company at US$4.5 billion.
Nvidia has also invested billions of dollars across the AI ecosystem since then, backing AI developers such as OpenAI. In January, the Financial Times reported that Hugging Face rejected a US$500 million investment offer from Nvidia last year that would have valued it at US$7 billion.
Nvidia's bet on strong AI demand was highlighted on Wednesday when it forecast a 70 per cent jump in revenue next fiscal year. It also said it has US$18 billion committed to equity investments through fiscal year 2027.
The report also comes a month after Hugging Face was hit by a security incident when an OpenAI model went rogue and triggered a hack that compromised Hugging Face infrastructure.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Japan's Nikkei reverses early gains as Nvidia supplier Advantest falls
Article:
TOKYO: Japan's Nikkei share average reversed early gains on Thursday, dragged down by Nvidia supplier Advantest, while the broader Topix inched higher on value-buying.
The Nikkei was down 0.14 per cent at 66,170.13, as of 0204 GMT, while the broader Topix rose 0.19 per cent to 4,118.69.
The Nikkei opened higher after chip company Nvidia shares rose nearly 5 per cent in extended trading following a forecast that revenue would jump 70 per cent next fiscal year.
The index changed course as chip-testing equipment maker Advantest erased its gains to trade lower. Advantest was last down 1.96 per cent. Technology investor SoftBank Group eased 0.56 per cent.
"The markets remain cautious about buying chip-related stocks after a sharp rise in the first half of this year," said Kazuaki Shimada, chief strategist at IwaiCosmo Securities.
"However, market sentiment is firm because the Topix rose, signalling the money was shifted to value stocks."
Banks rose, with Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group and Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group up 0.5 per cent and 0.7 per cent, respectively.
Fibre optic cable maker Fujikura rose 2.83 per cent and memory chip maker Kioxia was up 5.16 per cent.
Of the more than 1,500 stocks trading on the Tokyo Stock Exchange's prime market, 47 per cent rose, 48 per cent fell and 4 per cent traded flat.

Title: Kedah PKR hits out at Sanusi over remarks on gambling licences
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kedah PKR has hit out at Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor for hurling insults at Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim over the issue of gambling premises licences in the state.
Its communications director Tunku Nashrul Abaidah said Sanusi should instead answer for his administration's defeat based on the facts and stop making the prime minister a target.
"The fact is that Sanusi, as the menteri besar who led the administration in making the decision, lost in the legal action over the matter.
"His administration's decision was overturned after the court found that it had exceeded the state's jurisdiction.
"An application for leave to appeal was also rejected by the Federal Court," he said in a statement today.
Tunku Nashrul said Malaysia practises the separation of powers among the legislative, executive and judiciary, adding that the prime minister had no role in determining the court's decision.
"This case stemmed from a decision made by Sanusi's administration, which was challenged by the operator and decided independently by the judiciary.
"Sanusi should not throw stones and hide his hand. His hypocrisy and pretence of being holier than thou over this issue clearly reflect political hypocrisy.
"The reality is that when Pas was in the Perikatan Nasional government, the administration involving the party increased the number of special gambling draws from eight to 22 times a year.
"In contrast, it was Anwar, the prime minister and Finance Minister whom Sanusi insulted, who reduced it back to eight times a year," he said.
Tunku Nashrul also criticised Sanusi for allegedly misleading the public and dragging unrelated parties into the issue to cover up the shortcomings of his own administration.
"Sanusi should not move the goalposts. Answer for your administration's defeat based on the facts and stop making the prime minister a target," he said.
It was reported that Sanusi said Anwar would face the wrath of Kedahans if he allowed gambling activities to resume in the state.
"Kedahans will curse you if you approve it. In Kedah dialect, we call it 'pelaq'," he was quoted as saying.
On Aug 12, the Federal Court dismissed the Kedah government's application for leave to
appeal
against a Court of Appeal ruling declaring its ban on business licences for gaming operators unconstitutional.
In December last year, the appellate court, by a 2-1 majority, upheld the Alor Star High Court ruling, declaring the Kedah government's decision to cease the issuance and renewal of business licences for gaming operators unconstitutional and in violation of the Federal Constitution.
From Jan 1, 2023, legal gaming and lottery outlets in Kedah effectively ceased operations following the implementation of the state government's ban.
In November 2021, Sanusi announced that the state government would not approve new gaming licences or renew existing ones once they expired.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Anwar orders immediate aid coordination following Nepal, India flood disaster
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has ordered relevant authorities to immediately coordinate assistance following the devastating floods in Nepal and India.
"I have asked all agencies, including the National Security Council and the Foreign Ministry, to immediately assess the situation and contact our embassies in India and Nepal to expedite efforts to assist those affected," he said after opening the 2026 National Innovation and Commercialisation Expo at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre today.
The directive comes amid concern over
more than 50 Malaysian travellers in Nepal
who have been unreachable by their families since yesterday's floods, which have left hundreds of locals and foreigners unaccounted for.
Malaysian Embassy charge d'affaires in Kathmandu Mohd Firdaus Azman said damaged communication infrastructure and disrupted road access had made it difficult to obtain information on the Malaysians.
Nepalese authorities have deployed helicopters for search-and-rescue operations, although access to some affected areas remains difficult.
The floods, triggered after the collapse of part of a Himalayan glacier sent ice, rocks and mud into the river system, have so far killed more than 150 people and left hundreds of locals and foreign visitors unaccounted for.
Villages, bridges, roads and power projects were swept away, while flood alerts were also issued in parts of India as authorities monitored rising river levels downstream.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] 'Was he invited?': Anwar rubbishes Azmin Ali's refusal to rejoin PKR
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today took a jab at former PKR deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali after the latter ruled out returning to the party.
"Did anyone invite him? Was there an offer? I was not informed," Anwar told reporters after opening the 2026 National Innovation and Commercialisation Expo at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre today.
When reminded that he had spoken of welcoming otai (veterans) of the 'Reformasi' movement back into PKR, Anwar quipped: "Yes, otai. Is he (Azmin) an otai?"
On Tuesday, Azmin, who is now
Bersatu secretary-general
, said he would not return to PKR and remained committed to his present party.
He was responding to speculation over a possible return following Anwar's remarks that PKR's doors remained open to the party's former leaders.
Azmin was among PKR's most prominent figures and served as its deputy president before being expelled from the party in February 2020.
His expulsion followed his involvement in the political realignment dubbed the Sheraton Move, which brought down the Pakatan Harapan government led by then prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad.
Azmin subsequently
joined Bersatu
and is now a member of its Supreme Council.

Title: High airfares force Sabahans to cancel trips, miss funerals
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Airfares between the peninsula and Sabah and Sarawak, which have surged by more than 200 per cent, are placing a growing burden on Malaysians working in the peninsula, particularly those from the B40 group.
The high fares have forced some Sabahans to cancel trips for emergencies, including attending family funerals, while others have been stranded in their hometowns because they cannot afford return flights to the peninsula.
Members of the public are calling on the government and airlines to find an immediate solution and bring fares down to more reasonable levels.
Checks over the past two weeks found that some airlines were charging up to RM2,000 for one-way tickets on certain dates, while the lowest fares were around RM600.
Housewife Nur Sarina Saleh, 47, who lives in Selangor, said she and her three school-going children had been stranded in Sandakan, Sabah, for almost two months because they could not afford to spend thousands of ringgit on flights.
"I do not work, while my husband only has a regular job in Kuala Lumpur earning RM2,000 a month.
"We returned to our hometown in early July to visit my sick mother. We never expected to be still stranded here because tickets for the four of us cost more than RM3,000.
"So, my three children have also been out of school for almost two months because we are still stranded in our hometown. My husband has asked us to wait until the fares become slightly cheaper before returning.
"I do not know how we are going to get home. I cannot see a way for us to return to Kuala Lumpur," she said.
Private-sector employee Muhammad Ehsanulhadi Karim, 42, said he spent RM2,500 on a return flight between Kota Kinabalu and Kuala Lumpur at the end of July after a close relative died.
"The ticket from Kota Kinabalu to Kuala Lumpur alone cost RM1,500 per person, while the return ticket was RM1,000.
"If I had brought other family members, I would have had to spend thousands of ringgit more on airfares alone.
"People are told to buy tickets early to get cheaper fares, but in emergencies such as a death in the family, we have no choice but to pay thousands of ringgit," he said.
Ehsanulhadi said airfares should be reviewed, taking into account both airlines' operating costs and the burden on consumers.
"If airfares have to increase, perhaps RM400 to RM600 for a return trip would be reasonable. Why not reintroduce cheap-ticket promotions and ensure last-minute fares are not too burdensome for consumers?" he said.
Private-sector employee Nurul Syazwani Alias, 30, who lives in Sabah, said she and her family had to give up plans to attend her father-in-law's funeral in Kuala Lumpur because airfares were too expensive.
She said the one-way fare for three people had reached RM4,900 at the time.
"Imagine if we had to travel both ways, I would have needed more than RM8,000.
"We could not afford it, and I was so sad that I could not see my late father-in-law for the last time simply because airfares were too high.
"So, even if the government cannot directly control airfares because they depend on the airlines, it should consider other measures, including regulating how fares are set. Airlines should not be allowed to increase prices as they please," she said.
Pertubuhan Kebajikan Anak Sabah Kami Bersatu Selangor president Sudin Labiding said fares of up to RM2,000 were placing a heavy burden on Sabahans living away from home.
"Airfares are currently very expensive and burdensome for Sabahans living away from home.
"The government has previously fought against expensive airfares, so do something to bring them down to a reasonable level and ease the burden on ordinary Malaysians," he said.
Mountain-hiking operator Amanda Omeychua said her business had suffered losses of up to 40 per cent since July after some large groups cancelled their trips following increases in package prices linked to higher airfares.
"When airfares are too high, some customers have to postpone their trips, change dates or cancel their plans.
"For tourism operators like us, it is difficult to offer affordable packages even though our land-based operating costs can still be controlled," she said.
Meanwhile, Universiti Pendidikan Sultan Idris Ikatan Sepadu Anak Jati Sabah Supreme Council president Wagner Naftley Daniel said high airfares remained a concern among students, particularly those facing financial constraints.
He said students travel home not only during festive seasons and semester breaks but also for family matters, personal commitments and emergencies.
"We are worried because the new semester begins at the end of September. If fares remain at their current levels, how will students who are now back home return to the peninsula?
"We hope the RM600 Subfly subsidy channelled to public universities by the Sabah government and the RM400 Flysiswa subsidy provided by the federal government can be increased," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Peculiar', Ismail Sabri's lawyer says of charge against ex-PM
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob's lawyer has described the
charge against the former prime minister
as "peculiar", claiming it involved the same subject matter previously dealt with under a separate provision of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act.
Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad told the Sessions Court today that the defence would scrutinise the charge and reserved the right to challenge its propriety and validity.
He raised the matter when arguing for lower bail before Sessions Court judge Suzana Hussin.
Amer said that the prosecution had previously filed an application under Section 41 of the MACC Act involving the same subject matter.
Under Section 41, property seized under the Act may be dealt with by the court upon application by the prosecution, including cases where no prosecution is instituted.
The senior lawyer said that prior to invoking Section 41, a declaration had been made following a review of the investigation papers that no prosecution would be pursued.
"Unknown to us, for a very strange reason, despite exercising and using the power under Section 41, we now appear before this court saying that they (prosecution) are now going to prosecute my client for the very same subject matter that had been disposed of previously.
"I am raising this issue to put my learned friends on notice and to inform this court that we will be looking into this charge carefully," he said.
In July last year, the MACC applied to the Sessions Court to forfeit more than RM169 million seized during investigations.
On Oct 1, the Sessions Court ordered the money forfeited to the government after no third party claimed an interest in the funds or objected to the forfeiture.
Amer also questioned the prosecution's request for RM500,000 bail, pointing out that both parties had previously discussed a RM100,000 figure.
"The amount they are now proposing before this court is clearly made in bad faith.
"Previously, on the first date when the charge was registered before the court, we had discussed and communicated between the parties that the proposed amount of bail would be RM100,000," he said.
He argued that under Section 389 of the Criminal Procedure Code, bail should not be punitive or excessive and served only to secure the accused's attendance in court.
Deputy public prosecutor Farah Ezlin Yusop Khan had earlier asked the court to set bail at RM500,000 and order Ismail Sabri to surrender his passport.
Judge Suzana fixed bail at RM300,000 with one surety and rejected the prosecution's request for Ismail's passport, ruling that there was no evidence he was a flight risk.
Earlier, he pleaded not guilty to failing to comply with an MACC notice to declare assets under Section 36(2) of the MACC Act.

Title: FFB recovery may drive Hap Seng's second-half performance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Hap Seng Plantations Holdings Bhd may see stronger earnings in the second half of the year as fresh fruit bunch (FFB) production recovers seasonally and crude palm oil (CPO) prices remain supportive.
RHB Research said Hap Seng Plantations' second quarter ended June 30, 2026 (Q2 FY26) earnings were within its and consensus expectations, with first-half core earnings rising 12 per cent year-on-year (YoY) to RM77.7 million.
The improvement was mainly driven by a 23 per cent increase in CPO sales volume, alongside higher average selling prices (ASPs) for CPO and palm kernel.
RHB Research expects FFB production to strengthen in the second half, in line with Hqp Seng Plantations' guidance that production would peak in the fourth quarter.
Its FFB output fell seven per cent quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) and one per cent YoY in Q2, which the firm attributed to seasonal yield trends and changes in cropping patterns rather than structural operational issues.
On a seven-month year-to-date basis, however, FFB production rose 6.8 per cent YoY, although this remained below management's full-year growth target of 16 to 17 per cent and RHB Research's 10 per cent forecast.
The firm therefore maintained its FFB production growth assumptions at 10 per cent, 5.2 per cent and 5.1 per cent for FY26 to FY28 respectively.
Meanwhile, Hap Seng Plantations' CPO ASP rose nine per cent QoQ and YoY to RM4,630 per tonne in Q2, while palm kernel ASP increased eight per cent QoQ and seven per cent YoY to RM3,723 per tonne.
Both prices were about two per cent above the Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB) reference prices, prompting RHB Research to retain its assumption of a three to four per cent premium to MPOB prices for FY26 to FY28.
RHB Research expects CPO unit costs to improve in the second half as higher FFB production allows for better fixed-cost absorption.
It noted that the potential impact of a strong to very strong El Nino would likely only be felt from FY27, given the typical six to 12-month lag.
The firm made no changes to its earnings forecasts pending Hap Seng Plantations' analyst briefing on Aug 28, but raised its FY27 and FY28 CPO price assumptions to RM4,500 and RM4,400 per tonne respectively, from RM4,300.
It also rolled forward its valuation base year to FY27.
RHB Research maintained its "Buy" call on Hap Seng Plantations and raised its target price to RM2.95 from RM2.60.
At the new target price, the stock would be valued at 11.6 times FY27 forecast earnings, at the lower end of its peer range of 11 to 15 times.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal floods: Social media update eases sister's fears over sibling
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A sister's concern over the whereabouts and safety of her younger sibling, who is currently travelling to Annapurna Base Camp in Nepal, was eased after a social media user in the trekking area said conditions there were safe.
Threads user Iffarina had earlier appealed to the public to pray for her sibling's safety after she was unable to make contact, adding that she had contacted the Malaysian Embassy in Nepal for clarification.
She said her sibling's name was not on the list of missing persons, but she was still unable to reach her, believed to be due to communication problems in the area.
Her concerns were eased somewhat after another Threads user, Muhammad Hafizal Hamidon, a freelance tour guide, responded to her post, saying he was currently in the Annapurna Base Camp trekking area.
"I'm currently at the Annapurna Base Camp trekking area. Everything is fine here. Maybe she doesn't have internet," he said.
The response brought some relief to Iffarina and her family, although her sibling's condition could not be confirmed directly until communication is restored.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Shein set to raise US$1.7bil in Hong Kong IPO, sources say
Article:
HONG KONG: Online fast-fashion retailer Shein is set to price its shares at the middle of its marketing price range to raise HK$13.6 billion (US$1.73 billion) in its Hong Kong initial public offering, according to two sources with knowledge of the matter.
Shein, which is headquartered in Singapore and was founded in China, launched its long-awaited Hong Kong listing on Monday, offering 280 million shares at between HK$47.60 and HK$49.50 each.
The offering is expected to be priced at HK$48.56 a share, the sources said, speaking on condition of anonymity as the information is not yet publicly available.
Shein did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
