Title: Rare sight at KL court as Najib, Muhyiddin and Ismail Sabri appear for separate cases
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — The Kuala Lumpur Court Complex today saw the rare simultaneous appearance of three former prime ministers, each attending separate court hearings.
The unusual convergence brought together Datuk Seri Najib Razak, Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin and Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob at the same court complex, although their respective cases were unrelated.
Najib is expected to resume proceedings in the ongoing US$5.64 billion civil suit filed against him by 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) at the High Court.
Former Prime Minister, Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin after arriving at the Kuala Lumpur High Court Complex. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
In the suit, 1MDB and its subsidiaries accused Najib of breach of trust, breach of statutory duty, abuse of power and conspiracy to misappropriate 1MDB funds.
Separately, Muhyiddin is also attending his ongoing corruption trial linked to the Jana Wibawa programme, which is being heard at the High Court.
In the trial, Muhyiddin is facing seven charges, namely four counts of alleged power abuse to obtain RM225.3 million in bribes for his party, Bersatu, from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd, and three counts of alleged money laundering involving money that Bersatu received from Bukhary Equity.
Former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob Ismail Sabri was in court to face a charge over his alleged failure to declare his assets as required by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC). — Picture by Firdaus Latif
Ismail Sabri was also in court to face a charge over his alleged failure to declare his assets as required by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC).
According to the charge, Ismail Sabri is accused of failing to declare local and nine foreign currencies, as well as five gold bars (Suisse Fine Gold).
Among the currencies allegedly not declared were RM14.7 million, S$6 million, US$1.46 million, three million Swiss francs, €12.2 million, ¥363 million, £50,250, NZ$44,600, 34.8 million dirhams and A$352,850.
He later pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

Title: The Times frontman recalls last conversation with late guitarist, urges dashcam witnesses to come forward
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Naza Mohamad, the frontman of local indie band The Times, is urging those with dashcam footage of a recent hit-and-run involving their late guitarist to come forward to assist with the police investigation.
Speaking to local media during the 2 Konsert 2 Generasi press conference in KL yesterday, Naza revealed that their former bandmate Nazreen Sharkawi, 51, passed away on Aug 24 at Miri General Hospital, four days after falling into a coma following a hit-and-run accident in Miri, Sarawak.
“We still don’t know who hit him or what kind of car it was. If anyone in Miri has dashcam footage, please share it.
“It’s so sad for the victim — a hit-and-run like this is terribly unfair to them and their family,” Naza said, adding that Nazreen was riding his motorcycle when the accident happened.
Nazreen, affectionately known as Ein, was the rhythm guitarist for The Times from 2003 to 2007. He was also involved in producing the band’s first three albums before moving back to his hometown in Kuching after accepting a job there.
He was also the first cousin of Radhi from OAG, who was present during his funeral procession in Kuching recently.
View this post on Instagram
Recalling his last conversation with Nazreen, Naza said he was surprised to receive a call from him wanting to catch up with him and the band.
“It was a surprise because we hadn’t talked with each other for a while and he called me to ask how the band’s doing and said that he missed playing with the band.
“He also asked about our new album and The Times’ t-shirt that has his face on it and I told him I will send the album and t-shirt to him in Kuching.
“However, I’m a bit sad because I forgot to pass the items to my brother who went to Kuching recently and it turns out that was our last conversation. It’s as if he was giving us a sign but it went unnoticed at the time,” Naza said.
Naza added that Nazreen was loved by fans and friends for his humble and easy-going traits, and said he was also touched to see fans paying their respects to the late guitarist on social media.

Title: ‘Was there an invitation?’ Anwar questions Azmin’s claim he was invited back to PKR
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today appeared to question whether former PKR deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali was among the former party leaders and reformists he had invited to return to the party.
“Was there an invitation? I was not informed,” Anwar told reporters after launching the National Innovation and Commercialisation Expo (Nice 2026) at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre here.
Anwar was responding to a question about Azmin’s decision not to rejoin PKR following his recent call for veterans or “otai Reformasi” to return to the party.
Azmin, who left PKR in 2020 following the political crisis that led to the collapse of the Pakatan Harapan government, had reportedly ruled out returning to the party.
Anwar, who is also PKR president, had recently said the party’s doors remained open to former leaders and reformists who wanted to return and contribute to its reform agenda.
He was among several PKR leaders who left the party in February 2020, triggering the political upheaval known as the Sheraton Move.

Title: Anwar orders National Security Council, Nadma and Foreign Ministry to step up aid for Malaysians in India, Nepal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed the National Security Council (MKN), National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) and Foreign Ministry to immediately coordinate efforts to assist Malaysians affected by the situation in India and Nepal.
Anwar said he had instructed the relevant agencies to identify and contact Malaysian diplomatic missions in both countries to expedite assistance.
“I have instructed all relevant departments, including the National Security Council (MKN) and the Foreign Ministry, to immediately identify and contact our ministries and embassies in both India and Nepal to expedite efforts to assist them,” he told reporters after launching the National Innovation and Commercialisation Expo (Nice 2026) at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre here.
His remarks came as authorities in Nepal continued search and rescue operations following an earthquake triggered severe flash floods in a border area between Nepal and Tibet on Wednesday, killing nearly 157 people in the Himalayan nation.
More than 50 Malaysian travellers in Nepal are still unreachable after the incident, Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu’s charge d’affaires Mohd Firdaus Azman told Bernama last night.
The floods swept through the Rasuwagadhi-Timure area, destroying roads, buildings and infrastructure and cutting off access to parts of the affected region.
Anwar, in a Facebook post following the incident, said the government was taking immediate steps to ensure the welfare and safety of Malaysians affected by the situation.
He also said the Malaysian diplomatic missions in the affected countries would be contacted to facilitate efforts to locate and assist Malaysians there.

Title: Anwar urges Malaysia’s tech sector to innovate without losing sight of values
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Malaysia must pursue advances in science, technology and artificial intelligence without losing sight of its values, culture and humanity, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today.
Speaking at the launch of the National Innovation and Commercialisation Expo (Nice 2026) at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre here, Anwar said Malaysia’s pursuit of new technologies should remain grounded in the needs and interests of the people.
“Do not forget about the problems and interests of the people. If we are a Madani country, I often emphasise science and technology. It may seem as though this is about reaching for the skies — new knowledge, science, modern technology and AI, as though these are all new things.
“So, we are reaching for the skies, but do not forget that we are Malaysians, we are human beings, and we live by values.
“Therefore, while we reach for the skies, we must remain rooted to the ground,” he said.
He also called for greater efforts in research and innovation, saying the country should move beyond simply producing goods domestically towards developing Malaysian innovations that could be commercialised and exported.
“As emphasised by the Ministry and in the Malaysia Plan, we say that it should not only be ‘Made in Malaysia’, but also ‘Made by Malaysia’,” he said.
Anwar said Malaysia must work to ensure its products could be produced more effectively while building cooperation networks with countries in both the East and West.
He said this would help Malaysia maintain its position as a trading nation with a strong industrial focus, while strengthening its ability not only to produce but also to export.
Nice 2026 brings together researchers, innovators, industry players and other stakeholders to showcase research, technologies and innovations with commercial potential.

Title: NSM missile row: Malaysia awaiting Kongsberg response to demands, says Defence Minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Malaysia is waiting for Norway’s Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace (KDA) to respond to its demands after the company cancelled the export licence for Naval Strike Missiles (NSM) to Malaysia, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said today.
“If there is any response from them, I need to consult with the government for further considerations and decisions,” he told reporters after launching the National Day celebration at the Defence Ministry here today.
“But, we are also working hard so that the ammunitions for our littoral combat ships (LCS) can be transported safely,” he added.
Malaysia had initially procured the NSM anti-ship missiles from KDA, but the delivery was abruptly cancelled this year despite Malaysia having settled almost 95 per cent of the contract value.
Malaysia has since suspended all new defence procurements from Norway.
In July, Chief of Defence Force General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said Malaysia would require at least two more years to acquire a replacement surface-to-surface missile system for the LCS.
France, Italy, Turkey and South Korea have been shortlisted as potential suppliers for the replacement missile system.

Title: Buloh Kasap rep Zahari Sarip sworn in as Johor state assembly Speaker
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI, Aug 27— Buloh Kasap assemblyman Datuk Zahari Sarip has been sworn in as the Johor state assembly Speaker following his appointment to the post.
The 59-year-old former Johor Agriculture, Agro-Based Industry and Rural Development Committee chairman was earlier proposed by Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi at the Johor state assembly sitting today.
The proposal was also supported by Bukit Permai assemblyman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor.
Zahari replaces Datuk Mohd Puad Zarkashi, who has held the Speaker position since the previous Johor state election in 2022.
Mohd Puad, who is at odds with the state Umno leadership, previously announced his departure from the party on June 25.
Zahari expressed his appreciation for the trust that the menteri besar had placed in him.
He said that he would carry out his duties with full responsibility and dedication.
Zahari, representing Barisan Nasional (BN), successfully defended the Buloh Kasap state seat in the recent Johor state election.
He garnered 14,054 votes to defeat his opponent, Rozy Razit from Pakatan Harapan (PH), who obtained 5,454 votes.
In the July 11 state election, BN retained its mandate in Johor after winning a super-majority of 48 out of 56 state seats.

Title: Malaysia tightens Thai border security, to appoint facilitators for southern Thailand peace talks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Malaysia has tightened security across its land borders with Thailand, especially across forest ranges, following recent attacks in the southern part of the country, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said today.
Mohamed Khaled said the armed forces are increasing surveillance at the borders to prevent insurgents from infiltrating into Malaysia and spreading the violence here.
“The government will never allow any parties resorting to violence and denying the peace process in southern Thailand to hide or seek refuge on Malaysian soil.
“And, we will give our full cooperation to Thai authorities to ensure that it does not happen,” Mohamed Khaled told reporters at the Defence Ministry here today.
He said Malaysia will also appoint facilitators for the peace talks between Thai authorities and insurgent groups since the country is familiar with the conflict and the stakeholders involved.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is expected to appoint the facilitators soon.
“The prime minister has asked us for suggestions (for facilitator candidates) and we have provided them.
“This is because our long-time facilitator (and former National Security Council director-general) Datuk Rabin Mohd Basir’s contract has also expired,” Mohamed Khaled explained.
A series of coordinated attacks in several southern provinces of Thailand since last weekend torched several government buildings and vehicles, injuring three people.
The decades-long insurgency between Barisan Revolusi Nasional (BRN) rebels and the Thai government has killed over 7,000 people since 2004, according to data from Deep South Watch.

Title: Defence minister: Malaysia ready to deploy humanitarian aid to flood-hit Nepal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — The Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) is ready to support humanitarian missions to Nepal that is battling massive flash floods, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said today.
“MAF can support humanitarian missions, if the government decides to do so, and we are ready to contribute our expertise and capabilities,” Mohamed Khaled told reporters after launching the National Day celebrations at the Defence Ministry today.
However, he told reporters to refer to the Foreign Ministry for updates on the missing Malaysian tourists.
An earthquake triggered severe flash floods in a border area between Nepal and Tibet on Wednesday, killing nearly 157 people in the Himalayan nation.
Hundreds of foreign tourists are also missing with damaged communications and infrastructures hampering rescue efforts.
More than 50 Malaysian travellers in Nepal are still unreachable after the incident, Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu’s charge d’affaires Mohd Firdaus Azman told Bernama last night.

Title: Ex-PM Ismail Sabri charged with failure to declare assets to MACC; pleads not guilty
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob was charged today with failing to declare his assets to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC).
The 66-year-old pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court.
He is accused of failing to declare local and nine foreign currencies, as well as five gold bars (Suisse Fine Gold).
Among the currencies allegedly not declared were RM14.7 million, S$6 million, US$1.46 million, three million Swiss francs, €12.2 million, ¥363 million, £50,250, NZ$44,600, 34.8 million dirhams and A$352,850.
He claimed trial after the charge, made under Section 36(2) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act, was read out to him.
Section 36(2) covers the offence of wilfully neglecting or failing to comply with the terms of a notice issued by the MACC to give a written statement on oath or affirmation on their assets.
If convicted, he can be punished with a maximum five-year jail term and a maximum fine of RM100,000.
Ismail Sabri was accused of having on February 7, 2025 at the MACC headquarters in Putrajaya, wilfully given a written statement on oath that did not comply with the terms of a MACC notice dated January 7 the same year that was served on him on January 10.
Deputy public prosecutor Farah Ezlin Yusop Khan prosecuted, while Ismail was represented by lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad.
The prosecution initially urged the court to set bail at RM500,000 and order for Ismail to surrender his passport.
However, Amer Hamzah urged the court to impose the minimum bail, arguing that the former prime minister was not a flight risk and that the proposed amount was made in bad faith.
Sessions Court judge Suzana Hussin later fixed bail at RM300,000 and allowed Ismail to retain his passport after finding there was no proof to suggest the accused posed a flight risk.
Case is fixed for mention on September 29.
Former Umno vice president Ismail Sabri, 66, is the Bera MP and was Malaysia’s ninth prime minister from August 2021 to October 2022.
The MACC had in February 2025 arrested four of Ismail Sabri’s officers, and also seized about RM170 million in cash and other currencies, 16kg of gold bars valued at RM7 million, jewellery, and luxury watches from his aide’s house.
Ismail Sabri had appeared at the MACC headquarters multiple times between March to May 2025 to give his statement.
On October 1, 2025, the Sessions Court had ordered over RM169 million in cash to be forfeited to the Malaysian government, as both Ismail Sabri and his aide did not challenge the forfeiture and no other party challenged the forfeiture.

Title: More than 80 Ismail Sabri supporters travel three hours from Bera to KL court complex
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — More than 80 supporters of former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob gathered outside the Kuala Lumpur Court Complex here this morning to show their support for him.
One supporter, who identified herself as Liza, 42, said they were residents of Bera, Pahang who travelled to the capital on two buses that left at about 4am, BuletinTV3 reported.
Most of them were understood to be members of the Bera Umno division.
“We started getting ready at home as early as 3am before leaving for the capital.
“We arrived at about 7am after a journey of nearly three hours by bus. Some also drove their own vehicles here.
“It is all to give moral support to our elected representative,” she told reporters.
Ismail Sabri, 66, who is also the Bera MP, arrived at the Sessions Court here at 8.32am to face charges under the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009.
The case is scheduled to be mentioned before Judge Suzana Hussin at 9am.
The former prime minister is expected to face a charge under Section 36(2) of the MACC Act 2009 relating to asset declaration.
Ismail Sabri was originally scheduled to be charged on August 7, but the proceedings were postponed to today after he was admitted to the National Heart Institute (IJN) for health reasons.
Suzana had previously postponed the reading of the charges and the recording of his plea to Aug 27 after lawyer Amer Hamzah sought a deferment, citing Ismail Sabri’s possible irregular heartbeat and a planned procedure to implant a pacemaker.
The former prime minister had previously been called several times to have his statement recorded in connection with an asset declaration he made to MACC.
MACC also seized RM170 million in cash in various foreign currencies and confiscated 16kg of pure gold bars estimated to be worth RM7 million as part of a corruption and money-laundering investigation involving him.
The seizures were made during searches of residences and an office believed to have been used as a “safe house”, following investigations into four of Ismail Sabri’s senior officers who were arrested in February 2025.

Title: Malaysia must watch the Israel –Turkey fault line in Syria closely too — Phar Kim Beng
Article:
AUG 27 — Malaysia has every reason to watch Gaza closely. But Kuala Lumpur should not allow the continuing tragedy there to obscure another potentially dangerous development: the growing strategic friction between Israel and Turkey.
Israel’s August 18 strikes on Syria’s Abu al-Duhur airbase in Idlib were militarily limited but strategically significant.
Eight strikes reportedly hit the runway and storage areas without causing casualties. The facility had been largely inactive for years.
What made the attack important was not simply what Israel bombed, but whom Israel appeared to be addressing.
Israel subsequently argued that Syria had been close to violating a security understanding by permitting Turkish troops to deploy at the airbase.
Ankara denied that Turkish forces were present and said its military cooperation with Syria was focused on training and the exchange of expertise.
Turkey strongly condemned the attack, describing it as an assault on Syria’s infrastructure, territorial integrity and unity.
Malaysia should take notice.
The Middle East is entering a phase in which regional rivalries increasingly overlap. Israel’s security concerns are no longer confined to Iran, Hezbollah, Hamas or other familiar adversaries.
Turkey’s expanding influence in post-Assad Syria is increasingly becoming part of Israel’s strategic calculations.
That creates an entirely different order of risk.
Turkey is not a non-state actor. It is a major military power, a member of NATO and one of the most influential states in the Muslim world.
Kurdish fighters from the Qamishli Brigade, part of the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) participate in a military parade in Qamishli on August 21, 2026. — AFP file pic
Ankara also possesses a sophisticated defence industry, including increasingly capable drone, missile and electronic-warfare technologies.
A confrontation between Israel and Turkey would therefore represent something qualitatively different from many of Israel’s previous military engagements.
Abu al-Duhur demonstrates how easily such a confrontation could begin unintentionally.
The airbase lies relatively close to Turkey. American special envoy Tom Barrack warned after the strike that Washington was working towards a deconfliction mechanism involving Turkey, Israel and Syria precisely because misunderstandings between heavily armed states could have serious consequences.
The danger is escalation through miscalculation.
An Israeli aircraft approaches Syrian territory. Turkish radar detects it.
Ankara is uncertain about the intended target. Defensive systems are activated. An aircraft is challenged or shot down. Israel retaliates.
A political dispute can suddenly become a military crisis.
This is precisely why Malaysia must analyse Israeli behaviour beyond the immediate Palestinian question.
Malaysia has longstanding political sympathy for Palestine and has consistently supported Palestinian self-determination.
Yet Malaysian diplomacy cannot afford to view every Middle Eastern development exclusively through that prism.
The regional security architecture itself is changing.
Turkey has emerged as one of the principal external supporters of Syria’s new government under President Ahmed al-Sharaa.
Ankara wants a stable Syrian state, greater control over security threats along its southern frontier and sufficient influence over Syria’s reconstruction.
Israel, meanwhile, appears determined to prevent the emergence of military infrastructure in Syria that could restrict its freedom of action.
These strategic objectives can collide even when neither country actively wants war.
This is particularly important because the United States has relationships with both countries.
Washington therefore finds itself attempting simultaneously to reassure Israel, maintain its NATO relationship with Turkey and stabilise Syria.
Indeed, Barrack described the Israeli strike as an unnecessary escalation, while subsequent reporting indicated that Washington was concerned about how easily the episode could have spiralled.
Malaysia should consequently encourage deconfliction rather than simply observe events from afar.
There are at least three reasons.
First, instability involving Turkey would reverberate throughout the Muslim world.
Ankara possesses political, economic and military weight considerably beyond Syria.
Second, Malaysia and Turkey maintain substantial diplomatic, economic, defence and educational ties.
Any serious Israeli-Turkish confrontation would inevitably create diplomatic pressures across the wider Muslim world.
Third, the episode reinforces an important principle for Malaysian foreign policy: the sovereignty and territorial integrity of states must remain central to international order.
Whatever Israel’s security concerns about potential Turkish deployments, repeated unilateral military attacks inside another state’s territory risk normalising a regional environment in which powerful countries increasingly determine acceptable security arrangements through force.
That precedent should worry Asean too.
Southeast Asia depends heavily on norms restraining stronger states from imposing security preferences militarily on weaker neighbours.
Malaysia cannot reasonably defend sovereignty and international law in Southeast Asia while treating their erosion elsewhere as strategically irrelevant.
There is also a larger lesson.
The Middle East is becoming increasingly multipolar. Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Iran, Israel, Pakistan, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates are all developing overlapping networks of influence, while China, Russia and the United States remain deeply involved.
Malaysia therefore needs a wider strategic map of West Asia.
Palestine remains indispensable to Malaysian diplomacy. But so too must Syria’s sovereignty, Turkey’s security concerns, Gulf stability and the prevention of conflicts among major regional powers.
Abu al-Duhur may ultimately be remembered as a relatively small military episode.
But small incidents sometimes reveal large geopolitical transformations.
Israel’s strike suggests that the strategic contest over Syria is increasingly becoming intertwined with the emerging Israel-Turkey rivalry.
Malaysia should watch this fault line carefully.
The objective should not be to choose another side in another Middle Eastern rivalry.
It should be to prevent yet another regional confrontation from becoming a war that nobody originally intended to start.
* Phar Kim Beng is professor of Asean Studies, and director at the Institute of International and Asean Studies, International Islamic University Malaysia.
** This is the personal opinion of the writer or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of Malay Mail.

Title: Sultan of Pahang’s sister Tengku Aishah dies, to be laid to rest with full honours
Article:
KUANTAN, Aug 26 — The sister of the Sultan of Pahang, Tengku Puteri Seri Kemala Tengku Datuk Seri Aishah Almarhum Sultan Ahmad Shah, passed away at 9.15 pm yesterday at a hospital in Kuala Lumpur.
Comptroller of the Royal Household of the Sultan of Pahang Major General Datuk Mohamed Zahari Yahya said the body of the deceased would be taken to the Pahang Royal Mausoleum, Pekan today be buried with full honours and ceremonies.
He said the deceased’s death was a great loss to the Pahang Royal Family, especially to the Sultan of Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri’ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah and Tengku Ampuan Pahang Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah.
“May Allah SWT shower his blessings upon the deceased’s soul, forgive all sins and mistakes, accept all acts of worship and good deeds that have been done throughout her life, and place the deceased’s soul among the righteous and in His heaven.
“Let’s all pray that the deceased’s soul will be with the righteous,” he said in a media statement last night. — Bernama

Title: Ismail Sabri arrives in court to face asset declaration charges
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob arrived at the Sessions Court here this morning to face charges related to his asset declaration.
The 66-year-old Bera MP arrived at about 8.30am before meeting several supporters who had gathered outside the court, Kosmo! Online reported.
The charges are expected to be read before Judge Suzana Hussin today.
His lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad yesterday confirmed that Ismail Sabri would appear in court to face the charges.
The proceedings, originally scheduled for August 7, were postponed to today after Amer Hamzah sought a deferment as his client was receiving treatment at the National Heart Institute (IJN).
Ismail Sabri had previously been called several times by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to have his statement recorded in connection with the asset declaration he made to the agency.
MACC also seized RM170 million in cash in various foreign currencies and confiscated 16kg of pure gold bars estimated to be worth RM7 million as part of a corruption and money-laundering investigation involving him.
The seizures were made during searches of residences and an office allegedly used as a “safe house” following investigations into four of Ismail Sabri’s senior officers, who were arrested in February 2025.

Title: Mohamad Hasan in Jeddah for OIC meeting on latest developments in Palestine
Article:
JEDDAH, Aug 27 — Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan arrived here today to attend the extraordinary meeting of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) today.
He arrived at King Abdulaziz International Airport at 5.45 pm and was welcomed by Malaysian Ambassador to Saudi Arabia Datuk Syed Bakri Syed Abdul Rahman.
Mohamad is leading the Malaysian delegation to the one-day meeting, which will discuss the latest developments concerning Palestine, including the situation in Gaza and the West Bank, as well as the expansion of illegal Israeli settlements.
Syed Bakri had earlier said that Malaysia’s participation in the meeting is important in conveying the country’s firm position on Israel’s actions and aggression against Palestinian territories.
He said Mohamad would deliver National Statement, reaffirming the country’s unwavering support for the legitimate struggle of the Palestinian people and their right to establish an independent and sovereign state based on the pre-1967 borders.
The minister is also expected to meet his counterparts from several countries to discuss efforts to strengthen bilateral cooperation, including exploring new opportunities in business, trade and investment. — Bernama

Title: Mohamad Sabu: Malaysia must leverage technology, rural development to strengthen food security
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Malaysia needs to learn from China’s experience in strengthening the agricultural sector and food security through the use of technology, increased productivity and the development of rural areas that is planned in a systematic and continuous manner.
Minister of Agriculture and Food Security Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said Malaysia has great potential to continue strengthening the country’s agro-food sector by taking appropriate approaches based on the experiences of other countries, without neglecting the interests of local industry players.
“China has shown how the agricultural sector can be empowered through the use of technology, increased productivity, rural development and systematic and continuous planning.
“We need to dare to learn from the experiences of other countries, take an approach that suits our needs and at the same time continue to empower local farmers, rice farmers, livestock breeders and fishermen,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday.
Mohamad said he shared this in the Cabinet Meeting today as a result of his visit to China to attend the 11th Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Food Security Ministers’ Meeting in Hangzhou, recently.
He said at the same time, cooperation with other countries also needed to be further strengthened to ensure that the regional food supply chain remained strong and stable.
“The ultimate goal remains the same, which is to ensure that the people have enough food, the supply is guaranteed and the country has a more resilient food system to face future challenges,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Three foreign nationals arrested over alleged confinement of Chinese job seeker in Manjung
Article:
IPOH, Aug 27 — Three men, comprising a Japanese national and two Taiwanese nationals, were arrested by the police on suspicion of being involved in the wrongful confinement of a Chinese national in a premises at Venus Residence, near Seri Manjung, yesterday.
Manjung district police chief ACP Hasbullah Abd Rahman said the Manjung district police headquarters (IPD) operations room received a complaint from a 21-year-old victim via WhatsApp at around 10.30 pm, informing that he had been locked in the house.
He said a team of police from the Manjung IPD went to the scene of the incident at around 12.15 am yesterday and arrested all three suspects, aged between 21 and 33 years, while the victim, who was suspected of being unlawfully detained, was also rescued during the raid.
According to Hasbullah, initial investigations found that the suspects’ motive for doing so was because the victim refused to follow their orders, but the motive is still under further investigation.
“The three suspects and the victim are not known to each other. The victim was looking for a part-time job and got entangled with the suspects.
“The suspects and victim were taken to the Manjung IPD for further investigations, with the case being investigated under Section 342 of the Penal Code and Section (6)(1)© of the Immigration Act 1953/63,” he said, adding that all three suspects were remanded for four days until Aug 29.
Therefore, he said that members of the public who have information related to the incident are requested to come forward to the Manjung IPD, or contact the Manjung IPD operations room at 05-6886222 or WhatsApp the hotline at 017-6828005, or call at the nearest police station. — Bernama

Title: Sulong the elephant moves into Kelantan forest after days along Gerik-Jeli highway
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Sulong, the wild male elephant that drew attention after being spotted along the Gerik-Jeli East-West Highway (JRTB) in recent days, has now moved into a forested area in Kelantan.
Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) director-general Datuk Abdul Kadir Abu Hashim said monitoring showed Sulong was no longer detected along the JRTB towards Jeli, Kosmo! Online reported.
He said Perhilitan personnel had been deployed to monitor the elephant’s movements and condition using drones and regular ground patrols.
“Perhilitan is aware of the concerns raised by the public regarding this issue. Department personnel have been deployed to monitor Sulong’s movements and condition using drones, as well as through regular ground monitoring,” he said.
He said drones would be deployed at suitable locations to help track the elephant’s movements and location, alongside ground monitoring by Perhilitan personnel.
Abdul Kadir said any effort to rescue or handle Sulong could only be carried out once the elephant was in a suitable and safe location.
“This is important to ensure that the action taken does not pose additional risks to the elephant or compromise the safety of the operation personnel and the public,” he said.
He also urged motorists to follow instructions from enforcement personnel and Perhilitan officers and refrain from taking photographs or videos of the elephant, as stopping vehicles could disrupt traffic flow.
He said members of the public were also prohibited from feeding Sulong or leaving food for the animal along the JRTB.

Title: RON97, unsubsidised RON95 and diesel prices up 5 sen per litre
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — The retail prices of RON97, unsubsidised RON95 and unsubsidised diesel will each increase by 5 sen per litre for the Aug 27 to Sept 2 period.
The Ministry of Finance (MOF) said RON97 will be priced at RM4.30 per litre, up from RM4.25, while unsubsidised RON95 will increase to RM3.82 from RM3.77 and unsubsidised diesel to RM4.72 from RM4.67.
Meanwhile, the price of subsidised RON95 under Budi Madani RON95 (BUDI95) remains at RM1.99 per litre, while subsidised diesel under Budi Madani Diesel (BUDI Diesel) remains at RM2.10 per litre.
The prices under the Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS) and Subsidised Diesel Control System (SKDS) also remain unchanged at RM2.05 and RM2.15 per litre, respectively.
MOF said the government bears a subsidy of RM1.83 per litre for eligible consumers under BUDI95, equivalent to about 48 per cent of the current unsubsidised RON95 price.
For BUDI Diesel, the subsidy borne by the government is RM2.62 per litre, or 56 per cent of the unsubsidised diesel price.
MOF said prolonged global geopolitical uncertainty continued to put pressure on global petroleum prices and supply, with Brent crude oil prices remaining above US$90 a barrel for most of the Automatic Pricing Mechanism (APM) calculation period.
It said ongoing restrictions on traffic in the Strait of Hormuz continued to constrain global oil supply, while disruptions to refining capacity in West Asia and Russia reduced the supply of refined petroleum products, increasing the risk of further price pressures.
“After 179 days of conflict between the United States, Israel and Iran, around 290 million of the 400 million barrels of oil agreed to be released from the emergency reserves of International Energy Agency (IEA) member countries has been channelled to the market as of July 2026.
“The depletion of this supply buffer increases the risk of price pressures should disruptions continue,” it said, adding that the situation was putting greater pressure on diesel prices amid an increasingly tight global diesel market.
“Although global crude oil prices dropped at the end of the APM calculation period, the decrease was not sufficient to offset the higher price levels for most of the previous week.
“As long as petroleum flows through the Strait of Hormuz have not returned to normal and geopolitical uncertainty continues, the prices of petroleum products are expected to continue experiencing significant fluctuations in the near term,” it said. — Bernama

Title: Ramanan: Malaysia to steer Asean green jobs agenda, focus on skills for future workforce
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Malaysia remains the leader of the Asean green jobs agenda for the 2026-2030 period, having been entrusted to lead regional projects related to the field under the new work programme of the Asean Labour Ministers.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said this role was established through the Asean Labour Ministers’ Work Programme 2026-2030, thus continuing the mandate given to Malaysia in driving the green jobs agenda since chairing the Asean Labour Ministers’ Meeting (ALMM) and the Senior Labour Officials Meeting (SLOM) in 2018.
“The transition to a green economy cannot be viewed solely from an environmental or investment perspective. We must ensure that the Asean workforce possesses the necessary skills to fill the new jobs that will be created.
“At the same time, this transition must be implemented fairly and inclusively so that no workers or groups in society are left behind by the ongoing economic changes,” he said in a statement yesterday.
He said this while delivering Malaysia’s intervention at the 29th Asean Labour Ministers’ Meeting (ALMM) held at Dusit Thani Bangkok, Thailand yesterday.
Ramanan said that two important documents regarding green jobs were successfully achieved as part of the outcomes of Malaysia’s Asean Chairmanship 2025, namely the Asean Framework and Action Plan (FAP) for a Just and Inclusive Transition to Green Jobs 2025-2030 and the Joint Statement on Actionable Plan for Green Jobs Towards a Sustainable and Inclusive Asean Workforce.
According to him, these documents provide strategic direction for Asean to manage workforce changes following the green economic transition, in addition to strengthening joint actions among member states in developing a workforce prepared to face future economic shifts.
Ramanan also highlighted Malaysia’s success in organising the Asean Green Jobs Forum (AGJF) 2025 in Putrajaya, which gathered more than 450 delegates focusing on the theme “AI, Digitalisation and Green Jobs”.
According to the minister, the forum successfully shifted regional discussions from mere policy to more concrete implementation planning.
Among the priorities identified were the joint development of an Asean green jobs and skills taxonomy that can be matched with the Asean Qualifications Reference Framework (AQRF), alongside leveraging artificial intelligence (AI) as a facilitator in training and skills development.
Also given attention was the modernisation of the Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) ecosystem through closer cooperation with industry, targeted environmental, social, and governance (ESG) support for micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), and ensuring that new job opportunities can also be utilised by women, youth, and informal sector workers.
Ramanan said these efforts are important to ensure that the green jobs agenda does not move in isolation, but instead becomes an integral part of Asean workforce development in facing technological changes, digitalisation, and industrial transformation.
In a related development, Malaysia expressed its support for the Philippines, which will host the Asean Green Jobs Forum 2026 in Manila this coming October.
Ramanan said the rotational hosting of the AGJF according to the Asean Chairmanship is a positive development as it makes the green jobs agenda a shared responsibility among member states.
Malaysia previously hosted the AGJF in 2024 and 2025.
“Malaysia is ready to cooperate closely with the Philippines to ensure that AGJF 2026 produces meaningful actions in the implementation of the Asean Framework and Action Plan 2025–2030,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Haze: Four areas in Sarawak, capital record unhealthy API readings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Three areas in Sarawak and one in Kuala Lumpur recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in the unhealthy range as of 7.30am today.
Based on data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Samarahan recorded the highest API reading in Sarawak at 164, followed by the Serian District Police Headquarters (162) and Sri Aman (155).
Meanwhile, Cheras in Kuala Lumpur recorded an API reading of 129.
A total of 61 monitoring stations recorded moderate readings, while two stations recorded good readings.
No stations recorded readings in the very unhealthy or hazardous categories.
Meanwhile, API data for Politeknik Kota Kinabalu, Sabah was unavailable.
API readings are issued hourly based on data from 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide.
The public can obtain the latest air quality information through the Department of Environment’s official channels via eqms.doe.gov.my or the MyJAS EQMS app on Google Play and the App Store.

Title: Anwar: Give university students full freedom to voice views, foster critical thinking
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim stressed that university students must be given full freedom without restrictions that could impede their activities or prevent them from voicing their views at institutions of higher learning.
He said this was important to ensure universities once again serve as platforms for critical thinking and fresh perspectives in addressing the challenges facing education today.
Anwar said university managements and the relevant ministry must recognise that students should be given full freedom to foster a more dynamic intellectual culture.
“We must accept that university students should be given full freedom without restrictions that hinder their activities. Whether we agree or disagree is another matter...we can debate and challenge students to defend their arguments.
“But universities must be a platform for critical and fresh thinking,” he said at the Malaysia Madani Scholars Forum Series 13 at Dewan Tunku Canselor, Universiti Malaya, here last night. — Bernama

Title: Zambry: Comprehensive review of higher education laws needed to keep ecosystem relevant
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — The future of the country’s higher education requires a comprehensive review of acts related to higher education, including the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU).
Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir said the move to review and improve the existing legal framework are important to ensure that the higher education ecosystem remains relevant and is not further constrained by old regulations.
“We need to review the existence of acts related to higher education...among the acts that are always in focus is of course, AUKU itself.
“We admit that there are constraints that existed before. That is why we are looking at new aspects, including in terms of guaranteeing academic freedom, freedom of expression, and student empowerment,” he said here yesterday,
He said this as a panelist at the Madani Malaysian Scholars Forum Series 13, National Future Education and the Universities and University College Act (AUKU) at Dewan Tunku Chancellor, University of Malaya tonight, which was also attended by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
The forum also featured Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek and president of the Academy of Sciences Malaysia Tengku Datuk Mohd Azzman Shariffadeen as panelists, while Anwar acted as the moderator.
Meanwhile, Zambry said the Ministry of Higher Education (KPT) was also considering the drafting of a new act such as One Higher Education Act to coordinate various acts related to higher education under a more comprehensive framework.
To realise this, he said an Independent Committee had been established to collect and evaluate various memorandums and views from academics and student representatives.
Meanwhile, Fadhlina said the Ministry of Education (MOE) is committed to expanding access to the country’s education system through a ‘humane education’ approach to ensure that every child gets an equitable learning opportunity.
She said MOE has always adhered to the principle that access to education must reach all students regardless of location or where they are.
“Humane education was born to tap into the various talents and potentials of our children. That is why initiatives such as Schools in Hospital (SDH), schools in rehabilitation centres and the K9 and K11 School models for Orang Asli students continue to be strengthened.
“At the same time, access to pre-schools has also been expanded on a large scale for free because education starts at an early stage, in addition to helping ease the financial burden of families,” she said.
Fadhlina said the country’s education system should not be oriented solely on examination grades or simply providing human capital for the job market, but rather should focus on developing balanced, visionary individuals who have mental resilience and strong moral values.
“Children are not just numbers or exam grades. They come to school with intellect, emotions, ambitions and some come with anxieties or shortcomings that we need to address,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Anwar urges patience as govt works on comprehensive AUKU reforms for students
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim hopes that all university students and stakeholders can place their trust in the comprehensive improvement measures currently being planned by the government.
He said all parties need to give the government room to implement amendments or completely repeal the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU) for student freedom.
Anwar said he has personally been consistent in opposing the act for a long time, and emphasised the government’s current commitment to bringing about comprehensive change for the benefit of students and higher education institutions.
“Give us room, I have fought this act (AUKU) for a long time. Now we want to amend it comprehensively, so please give a little room,” he said when answering a question from a participant at the Malaysia MADANI Intellectual Forum Series 13 on the Nation’s Future Education and AUKU at the Dewan Tunku Canselor, Universiti Malaya, here last night.
The participant wanted to know what guarantees the government can provide that the new act replacing AUKU will not simply be AUKU in a new form.
Also present were Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abdul Kadir, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek, and Academy of Sciences Malaysia President Tengku Datuk Mohd Azzman Shariffadeen.
Elaborating further, Anwar said the effort to amend or repeal the act requires a comprehensive process and thorough review following discussions at the Ministry of Higher Education (KPT) and Cabinet levels.
The Prime Minister also gave assurances that the government is committed to providing broader political space and channels for freedom of speech for students, anchored on good governance and orderly laws.
Meanwhile, Anwar asked the National Student Consultative Council (MPPK) to give him a little time to hold a special meeting session to discuss matters raised by student representatives regarding the act’s validity and student welfare.
“Give (me) a little time. I am focusing on the Budget... then Independence Day, then Malaysia Day... it will be very challenging, but insya-Allah, I will,” he said.
Earlier, MPPK representatives submitted two matters to the Prime Minister: requesting that the MPPK, which comprises 35 student leader representatives from public universities (IPTA), polytechnics, and community colleges, be officially involved in the drafting or amendment committee of the act; and secondly, requesting a special premier meeting with the Prime Minister to voice core student issues directly. — Bernama

Title: Nepal floods: 17 Malaysians among hundreds still unaccounted for
Article:
HYDERABAD, Aug 27 — Seventeen Malaysians are among hundreds of foreigners missing following a devastating flash flood in Nepal’s Rasuwa district yesterday morning, according to Nepal’s tourism board.
The board said in a statement that the missing Malaysians were handled by the Fishtail Tours and Travels tour agency.
At least 291 foreigners and 93 Nepalese are uncontactable, and police and tour operators are trying to locate them, it said in a situation update in the afternoon.
The Malaysian Foreign Ministry said in a statement issued earlier that 11 Malaysian nationals believed to be in Rasuwa’s district had lost contact following the flood.
It said the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu was actively coordinating with local authorities.
“The search and rescue teams currently being deployed by the Nepalese government are working to locate the affected Malaysians and ascertain their safety,” it said.
The Bhote Koshi river flood has swept away many villages and destroyed roads, buildings and hydropower projects in the Rasuwagadhi-Timure area of Nepal.
Other foreigners who have lost contact include 142 Indians, including 37 Indian citizens living abroad, and many citizens of Britain, South Africa and the United States (US). — Bernama

Title: Budi95’s monthly limit: How far can 200 litres take you?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Is 200 litres of subsidised RON95 enough to get through the month?
That is a question some motorists are still asking after the government reduced the monthly Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) eligibility limit from 300 litres to 200 litres, effective April 1, 2026.
While RON95 fuel subsidised under Budi95 remains at RM1.99 a litre, the unsubsidised price for August 20 to 26 was RM3.77 a litre.
The Ministry of Finance (MOF) confirmed that the government bore RM1.78 a litre in subsidies for eligible users that week.
With households grappling with the rising cost of living, concern over whether 200 litres is enough is understandable.
So, how far does 200 litres go? It depends
How far 200 litres goes depends on the car, the distance travelled and how often it is used.
For a short daily commute, 200 litres could be more than enough, while a vehicle that spends much more time on the road could run out sooner.
Government data, however, shows that nearly 90 per cent of eligible Budi95 users consume less than 200 litres a month, with average monthly consumption at around 100 litres.
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan subsequently said actual Budi95 usage data from October 2025 to June 2026 showed that “fewer than one per cent of Budi95 users consistently consume more than 200 litres of RON95 per month.”
200 litres, different cars, very different distances
One way to understand the allocation is to look at manufacturers’ published fuel-efficiency figures.
Distances shown are calculations based on 200 litres and published fuel-efficiency figures from the manufacturers’ respective test cycles.
Actual fuel consumption varies with traffic, road conditions, air-conditioning, vehicle load and driving style.
What about everyday city driving?
Published fuel-efficiency figures are based on standardised tests and do not necessarily reflect stop-start Malaysian traffic.
For a more conservative illustration, assume a vehicle averages 10km per litre in city driving.
At that rate, 200 litres would cover about 2,000km.
For someone commuting 22 working days a month:
Route distances are approximate road distances.
Fuel use is calculated using an illustrative 10km/L city-driving assumption and 22 working days a month; actual consumption varies.
Someone travelling 100km a day for work could therefore theoretically use more than 200 litres before accounting for other trips.
A roughly 23km one-way road journey between Kuala Lumpur and Shah Alam would work out to about 101 litres a month at 10km/L, assuming a return trip on 22 working days.
These are illustrations rather than estimates of actual consumption for every driver.
What about those who use more than 200 litres?
Amir had said fewer than one per cent of Budi95 users consistently consume more than 200 litres a month.
Consumption can vary depending on distance travelled, location, vehicle type, traffic and whether driving is part of someone’s work.
For e-hailing drivers, MOF announced a tiered system under which drivers travelling 2,000 to 5,000km a month can receive up to 600 litres, while those travelling more than 5,000km can receive up to 800 litres.
When the ordinary Budi95 ceiling was reduced to 200 litres, MOF said the additional quota cap for e-hailing operators would remain at 800 litres a month.
Why not simply make petrol cheaper?
But if some motorists are concerned that 200 litres is not enough, why can’t the government simply spend more to subsidise more fuel — or make petrol cheaper?
Put simply, the government has said it cannot continue absorbing such high costs.
MOF said in March that subsidies for RON95 and diesel had amounted to about RM700 million in January 2026, while the bill was estimated to reach around RM4 billion a month as crude oil prices rose above US$100 (RM402) a barrel.
That volatility matters because the cost of keeping petrol subsidised is not fixed.
How much would it cost to increase the subsidy by one sen?
Treasury secretary-general Datuk Johan Mahmood Merican said Malaysia consumes about 18 billion litres of fuel a year, with households accounting for about 78 per cent of RON95 consumption.
If all 18 billion litres attracted an additional one sen of subsidy, the annual cost would be about:
18 billion litres × RM0.01 = RM180 million
An additional one sen of subsidy per litre would therefore represent roughly RM180 million a year, assuming consumption remained unchanged and all 18 billion litres attracted the additional subsidy.
That is a calculation based on the government’s consumption figure, not an official estimate of the cost of a one-sen price reduction.
Ten sen a litre would amount to about RM1.8 billion.
The calculation shows why a seemingly small change at the pump can become a substantial fiscal commitment when applied across billions of litres.
Where to draw the line
For an individual driver, another few sen of subsidy may not seem significant.
Across billions of litres of RON95, however, even a small increase in the subsidy can translate into hundreds of millions of ringgit in additional government spending.
That is the trade-off behind Budi95: keeping subsidised petrol affordable while limiting the fiscal cost of providing it to everyone.
Small ways to make fuel go further
Fuel consumption is not entirely within a driver’s control, as traffic, road conditions, vehicle type and distance travelled all matter.
But some simple habits can reduce unnecessary consumption:
Keep tyres properly inflated, as under-inflated tyres increase rolling resistance.
Avoid prolonged idling where practical and safe, as a stationary engine still consumes fuel.
Combine trips when convenient, as several separate journeys can add unnecessary kilometres.
Drive smoothly, as repeated hard acceleration and braking can increase fuel consumption.
Keep the vehicle maintained, as a properly serviced vehicle is more likely to operate efficiently.
Plan journeys, as combining errands and avoiding unnecessary detours can reduce the distance travelled.

Title: ‘The dream does not bode well’: Wan Junaidi recalls jungle operation that shaped his leadership
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 26 — “Nda manah  mimpi... anang baka nyak.”
The Iban phrase, meaning “The dream does not bode well... don’t do it” has remained etched in the memory of the Yang Dipertua Negeri of Sarawak Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar, even after more than 50 years.
Those were the last words uttered by Jungle Squad Constable Jabu Ajai before he was killed during an operation to hunt communist terrorists in Tulai, Sarawak, in 1971.
For Wan Junaidi, who was leading the team during the operation, the incident was more than just another episode in the line of duty. It was a deeply moving experience that taught him enduring lessons about responsibility, leadership and humanity.
Operation to hunt communists
Recalling the incident, Wan Junaidi said that, as an Inspector at the time, he was ordered to lead his platoon to a location to conduct a special operation after a team stationed at Tulai, Binatang (now Bintangor), came under an ambush.
The attack left two Jungle Squad personnel dead and six others seriously injured.
“After receiving a briefing in the operations room, my platoon left Sibu for the location at about 4 pm aboard a Nuri helicopter and spent the night near the area.
“I instructed my men that we had to move at 7 am the next morning because we could not spend two nights in the same place. We had to find those who had killed our men,” he told
Bernama.
The following morning, as all the personnel were preparing to move out, Jabu was still asleep.
“I wondered why Jabu had not got up. Then one of the men, Constable Merom Bujak, volunteered to wake him up the Gurkha way by kicking him until he woke up.
“Once awake, he told us he had a nightmare. But before I could ask him more about the dream, I ordered Jabu to get ready and delayed our movement by an hour. We finally set off at 8 am to begin the mission,” he said.
After about two hours of travelling, his team arrived in a hilly area, where a reconnaissance team alerted them to the suspicious movement of several individuals believed to have fled from a house nearby.
Wan Junaidi and his men proceeded to the house for further inspection. Inside, they found an elderly man, a woman and five children. Nothing appeared unusual, except for several cups of tea placed on the table.
“It was suspicious because children would not be drinking tea. Besides, there were far too many glasses on the table.
“I then instructed one of the men to check the hilly area behind the house. The search uncovered a resting place used by communist terrorists, confirming that the house had been used as a stopover for the communists to eat and drink before retreating to a strategic position on the hill,” he said.
Jabu's final mission
Wan Junaidi said he subsequently led his platoon up the hill, when suddenly gunfire erupted from the enemy’s direction.
In a split second, Jabu and Merom fell.
Wan Junaidi rushed to Jabu, who had died on the spot, while Merom was seriously injured.
“I can still vividly remember the blood gushing from Jabu’s body... I never imagined that his nightmare, which had left him feeling uneasy that morning, was a bad omen.
“After realising that Jabu had been killed, Corporal Majani, his close friend, rushed forward, embraced his body and wept, crying, ‘Why must you die?’,” he said, his voice filled with emotion.
According to Wan Junaidi, Majani, overwhelmed by grief and anger after seeing his close friend’s  body, wanted to kill all the civilians in the house.
“He acted rashly, returning to the house with the intention of killing the elderly man, woman and children there, while pointing a Bren light machine gun at them.
“Realising what Majani was about to do, I immediately rushed back to the house and kicked him to stop him from acting on his intention. I then ordered a member of the team, Hassan, to keep the situation under tight control.
“I told Hassan, ‘I have no time to deal with Majani. Don’t let him get hold of his weapon. Even though we know what their parents have done, we cannot kill these children,’” Wan Junaidi said firmly.
For him, the principles of humanity and the safety of civilians could never be compromised, even in the midst of battle and the loss of a fellow comrade.
Investigations later revealed that the elderly man was a key leader of the group responsible for managing the finances of communist terrorists in the area.
“Intelligence also revealed that the killing of the Jungle Squad personnel at Tulai Camp was carried out by a group from Ngemah led by Ubong Nuing,” he said.
Ubong Nuing was the leader of the North Kalimantan People’s Army (PARAKU),  an Iban who joined the communist armed movement in Sarawak opposed to the formation of the Federation of Malaysia in 1963, before surrendering to the authorities in the 1980s.
The jungle as a teacher
Wan Junaidi said his years serving as a Jungle Squad officer taught him the true meaning of discipline, emotional control and humanity while carrying the responsibility of defending the country.
He said the sense of camaraderie within his multi-ethnic platoon also changed the way he viewed situations, particularly as a leader who had to respect the views and beliefs of his men.
“In my platoon, when I was serving in Miri, half were Orang Ulu and the other half Iban, with only two or three Malays. In Sibu, the composition was slightly different, with most being Iban and a smaller number of Orang Ulu and Malays.
“That was where I learnt a great deal about the cultures and beliefs of my men. The Iban, for example, have certain beliefs about dreams, sounds and various other signs... I learnt about all these things so that I could understand my men,” he said.
Recalling another experience while serving in the jungle, Wan Junaidi said it taught him the importance of understanding his men’s beliefs, particularly when faced with critical situations.
He said it was around 7 pm and darkness was beginning to descend, but his platoon had yet to set up camp for the night.
“While we were putting up the tent, suddenly a tree branch fell near the spot where we intended to set up camp. After that, all my men fell silent.
“I did not know why they had suddenly stopped working. One of them came to me, spoke to me in Iban and explained their belief.
“The Iban believe that if you are doing something and something unexpected happens, it is a sign that misfortune is about to come,” he explained.
Wan Junaidi, who was only 23 at the time, realised that although he was the leader, he still needed to remain humble and respect the views of his men, particularly those who were much older and more experienced than him.
“I then asked how we could overcome the situation as it was almost dark, we had not eaten and the tent had yet to be completed.
“They said we could move elsewhere and did not have to go far. Although we had already gathered the wood and materials to put up the tent, I agreed and ordered everyone to move,” he said.
Realising that his men’s concerns could affect their concentration and morale, Wan Junaidi decided to move about 100 metres from the original location.
“Everyone was happy. If I had said we were staying there, they would not have been happy because, for them, it was not just about the leader dying. Many more could have been killed if a battle broke out.
“After we moved and put up the tent again, everyone became calm. A sergeant came to me and said, ‘Sir, you made a very good decision.’ Otherwise, the men would have been worried and unable to sleep,” he said with a smile.
From that experience, Wan Junaidi said a leader must not only know how to defend the country, but also understand the hearts, beliefs and concerns of his men.
“In the jungle, where uncertainty is everywhere, the strength of a team lies not only in its weapons, but in the confidence and trust they have in one another,” he said.
What shaped his leadership
Wan Junaidi’s experiences as a police officer were also documented in his 2014 book,
A Policeman,
which includes accounts of his encounters with the communist threat as well as historical information on the era of communist violence in Sarawak.
Born in Kampung Pendam (now Sadong Jaya), Sarawak, on Feb 1, 1946, Wan Junaidi, 80, joined the Royal Malaysia Police in 1964 and served in the Jungle Squad from 1968 to 1973, during which he was also posted to the Rajang Area Security Command (Rascom).
He subsequently pursued legal studies at the University of Buckingham, England, in 1978 before becoming a practising lawyer.
He later became actively involved in politics and administration, holding several key positions in the Federal Cabinet before being appointed President of the Senate.
He was appointed the Yang Dipertua Negeri of Sarawak for a four-year term from Jan 26, 2024 to Jan 26, 2028. — Bernama

Title: Anwar hails TM’s 80-year role in expanding connectivity, calls for shared prosperity
Article:
CYBERJAYA, Aug 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today praised Telekom Malaysia Bhd (TM) as an important institution in nation-building as it marked its 80th anniversary, saying the company had played a pivotal role in democratising communication across the country.
Anwar, speaking at the company’s anniversary celebration here ahead of the Merdeka celebrations on Monday, said TM had evolved from its pre-independence roots into a key driver of connectivity and digital development today.
“Independence is not merely about replacing English officers with Malay officers, nor is it about extracting wealth for the elite,” Anwar said.
“It is about sharing that prosperity with the people and from pre-independence until today, TM has provided essential connectivity, comfort, and developed to meet the evolving needs of the nation, for everyone,” he added.
Anwar also touched on TM’s privatisation in the 1990s, saying greater efficiency and profitability were important but should not come at the expense of workers’ welfare.
Anwar said he acknowledged that TM’s privatisation helped drive corporate efficiency and profits.
Still, he stressed that government-linked companies must balance financial performance with social responsibility, pointing to TM as a model for equitable growth under his “Madani” policy framework.
“We privatise for efficiency and profits, but it cannot be limited to just that,” Anwar noted, urging corporate leaders to focus on improving worker welfare, raising wages, and securing quality housing and education for employees’ families.
He said TM had an important role to play as Malaysia moves into a new era of technological development, including in areas such as artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies.
“If we want to progress, we must step into a new era and train our youth to explore new frontiers,” Anwar said.
He said TM is one of the service providers instrumental in that push, as the government looks to deploy next-generation internet-based capabilities and digital infrastructure.
He described TM as a regional powerhouse but stressed that technological progress and economic growth must ultimately benefit all Malaysians.

Title: Haze: Selangor local authorities told to step up monitoring, crack down on open burning
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 26 — All local authorities (PBT) in Selangor have been urged to step up monitoring to prevent open burning following unhealthy air quality recorded in several areas across the state.
State Public Health and Environment Committee chairman Jamaliah Jamaluddin said the move followed the activation of the National Haze Action Plan by the Department of Environment (DOE), approved by the Selangor State Executive Council (MMKN) at its meeting today.
She said strict action would be taken against those involved in open burning under Section 29(A) of the Environmental Quality Act 1974.
“If convicted, offenders can be fined up to RM1 million or jailed for up to five years, or both. They may also face an additional fine of up to RM5,000 a day for continuing offences after a notice has been issued,” she said in a statement today.
Jamaliah also urged the public to report any open burning activities through the Selangor DOE hotline at 1-800-88-2727 or via the DOE eAduan application.
She said Selangor state secretary Datuk Dr Ahmad Fadzli Ahmad Tajuddin would chair a State Disaster Management Committee meeting tomorrow to discuss further measures to reduce the impact of haze on the public.
Meanwhile, Jamaliah advised the public to minimise outdoor activities unless necessary, especially those with respiratory-related health issues.
“Schools statewide have been issued notices outlining precautionary measures to protect students, particularly those in areas where the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings exceed 100.
“Schools, kindergartens and childcare centres must be closed if API readings reach 200,” she said.
As of 8am today, 17 areas in six states and two Federal Territories recorded unhealthy API readings.
According to data from the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, five areas in Selangor recorded readings above 100 - Johan Setia and Shah Alam (158 respectively), Klang (151), Banting (144) and Petaling Jaya (123). — Bernama
